note: Abdon of Pirathon in Ephraim succeeds Elon and rules eight years.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 84

name: Shimshon becomes Shofet
note: Samson son of Manoach of Dan succeeds Avdon and begins his period of opposition to Philistine power.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 86

name: Angel announces Shimshon's birth and Nazirite status in the biblical narrative
note: Judges 13 describes Manoach's wife being told that her son is to live under special Nazirite restrictions.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 86

name: Shimshon seeks marriage with a Philistine woman at Timnah
note: The marriage episode becomes the setting for the first major series of conflicts with the Philistines.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 86

name: Shimshon kills a lion near Timnah
note: Judges 14 describes Samson killing a lion and later finding honey in its carcass.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 86

name: Shimshon's riddle leads to conflict at the wedding feast
note: The Philistine wedding dispute escalates into violence.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 86

name: Shimshon kills thirty men at Ashkelon
note: Judges 14 says Samson obtains garments for his wager by killing thirty Philistines at Ashkelon.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 86

name: Shimshon burns Philistine crops
note: Judges 15 describes retaliation involving foxes or jackals with torches set among Philistine grain and vineyards.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 86

name: Shimshon defeats Philistines at Lehi
note: After being handed over by men of Judah, Samson breaks free and kills a large Philistine force with a donkey's jawbone.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 86

name: Shimshon carries away the gates of Gaza
note: Judges 16 describes Samson escaping an ambush by carrying off Gaza's city gates.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 86

name: Shimshon and Delilah episode
note: Delilah repeatedly seeks the secret of Samson's strength until he reveals the role of his uncut hair and Nazirite identity.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 86

name: Philistines capture and blind Shimshon
note: After his hair is cut, Samson is seized, blinded and imprisoned in Gaza.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 86

name: Eli HaKohen becomes Shofet and Kohen Gadol
note: Eli succeeds Pinchas as Kohen Gadol and begins forty years of judgeship.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 86

name: Channah prays at Shiloh for a son
note: Channah prays at Shiloh for a son.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 86

name: Shmuel is born
note: Samuel is born in the same year Eli becomes leader.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 86

name: Channah dedicates Shmuel to service at Shiloh
note: The young Samuel is brought to the sanctuary to serve under Eli.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 86

name: Eli's sons abuse priestly authority in the biblical narrative
note: I Samuel describes Hophni and Phinehas corrupting sacrificial and communal life at Shiloh.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 86

name: Shmuel receives his prophetic call at Shiloh
note: The young Samuel hears the divine call and receives a prophecy concerning Eli's house.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 86

name: Shimshon dies destroying the Philistine temple in Gaza
note: Samson's death is dated to 2831; Judges 16 describes him pulling down the Philistine temple on himself and its assembled rulers.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 86

name: Philistine pressure is said to remain reduced after Shimshon's death
note: Philistine pressure is said to remain reduced after Shimshon's death.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 86

name: David ben Yishai is born
note: David ben Yishai is born.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 86

name: Codex links Ruth's ancestry to Eglon and Balak
note: Ruth's ancestry is linked to Eglon and Balak.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 86

name: Israel brings the Ark into battle against the Philistines
note: This was the only occasion on which this Ark was taken into battle.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 86

name: Philistines defeat Israel and capture the Ark
note: The Israelite army is defeated and the Ark is captured.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 86

name: Hophni and Phinehas are killed in battle
note: Eli's two sons die in the same Philistine victory.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 86

name: Eli dies after hearing that the Ark was captured
note: Eli's death is dated to 10 Iyar, with an alternate tradition placing it in the following year.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 86

name: Shiloh Mishkan is destroyed
note: The Mishkan at Shiloh is destroyed on the day Eli dies.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 86

name: Pessel Michah worship ends in Codex chronology
note: Worship associated with Micah's idol continues until the destruction of Shiloh.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 86

name: Ark is brought to Ashdod
note: I Samuel 5 describes the captured Ark being placed in the temple of Dagon at Ashdod.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 86

name: Dagon image falls before the Ark in the biblical narrative
note: The Philistine cult image is twice found fallen before the Ark.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 86

name: Ark is moved through Philistine cities
note: The Ark is transferred among Philistine centers as calamity is associated with its presence.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 86

name: Philistines decide to return the Ark
note: After seven months, Philistine leaders decide to send the Ark back with a guilt offering.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 86

name: Philistines return the Ark to Beit Shemesh
note: The Ark is returned after seven months in Philistine hands.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 86

name: Ark is transferred to Kiryat Ye'arim
note: After Beit Shemesh, the Ark is placed in the house of Avinadav at Kiryat Ye'arim.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 86

name: Ark begins a twenty-year stay at Kiryat Ye'arim
note: The Ark remains there for twenty years even while the Mishkan operates elsewhere.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 86

name: Mishkan is re-established at Nov
note: The sanctuary is reconstructed at Nov after Shiloh's destruction.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 86

name: Shmuel becomes national leader
note: Samuel, already accepted as a prophetic figure in Eli's lifetime, succeeds as the principal judge and leader.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 86

name: Shmuel calls Israel to repentance at Mizpah
note: I Samuel 7 describes a national gathering, fasting and rejection of foreign gods under Samuel.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 86

name: Philistines attack the Mizpah assembly
note: The gathering triggers a Philistine military response.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 86

name: Israel defeats the Philistines under Shmuel
note: Samuel's leadership is consolidated after an Israelite victory over the Philistines.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 86

name: Shmuel erects the Eben-Ezer memorial
note: Samuel sets up a memorial stone marking the victory and divine help.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 86

name: Shmuel establishes a circuit of judicial leadership
note: I Samuel 7 describes Samuel regularly judging Israel at Bethel, Gilgal, Mizpah and his home in Ramah.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 86

name: Shmuel appoints Yoel and Aviyah as regional leaders
note: Shmuel appoints Yoel and Aviyah as regional leaders.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 86

name: Israelite elders request a king
note: The people ask Samuel to appoint a king 'like all the nations', initiating the transition from the judges to monarchy.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 86

name: Shmuel initially opposes the request for monarchy
note: Samuel is displeased by the request and warns of the costs and powers of kingship.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 86

name: Shmuel warns the people about royal power
note: I Samuel 8 presents Samuel's warning that a king will conscript labor, appropriate resources and centralize authority.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 86

name: Pre-monarchic era reaches its endpoint
note: Pre-monarchic era reaches its endpoint.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 86

name: Shaul becomes the first king of Israel
note: Shaul becomes the first king of Israel.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 93

name: Shaul defeats Nachash the Ammonite and wins national acceptance
note: Shaul's victory over Nachash the Ammonite at Jabesh-Gilead establishes his authority beyond the initial anointing.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 93

name: Shmuel secretly anoints David
note: Shmuel secretly anoints David.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 93

name: David kills Goliath
note: David defeats Goliath and gains exceptional public fame.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 93

name: David marries Michal daughter of Shaul
note: Shaul gives David his daughter Michal after David's military success.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 93

name: Shaul's jealousy of David intensifies
note: David's popularity and closeness with Yehonatan fuel Shaul's hostility and pursuit.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 93

name: Shmuel dies
note: Shmuel dies.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 93

name: Codex attributes Shoftim, Ruth and Shmuel to Shmuel
note: Shoftim, Ruth and Shmuel is attributed to Shmuel.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 93

name: David marries Avigayil
note: After Shmuel's death, David marries Avigayil, widow of Naval.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 93

name: Shaul hunts David across the country
note: In the later part of Shaul's reign he repeatedly pursues David, who receives prophetic advice from Gad.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 93

name: Shaul and his sons are defeated at Mount Gilboa
note: Shaul sees three of his sons killed in the Philistine battle and dies as the kingdom collapses around him.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 93

name: David becomes king of Judah in Hebron
note: After Shaul's death, the thirty-year-old David is accepted as king over his own tribe of Judah and rules from Hebron.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 93

name: Mishkan at Nov is destroyed and worship shifts to Givon
note: The sanctuary at Nov is destroyed and rebuilt at Givon while the Ark remains at Kiryat Ye'arim.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 93

name: Avner installs Ish Boshet as king over northern Israel
note: During David's limited Hebron rule, Avner installs Shaul's son Ish Boshet over the rest of Israel.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 93

name: Ish Boshet is assassinated
note: After a short reign, Ish Boshet is killed and David punishes those responsible.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 93

name: All Israel accepts David as king
note: Following Ish Boshet's death, representatives of the tribes accept David as king over all Israel.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 93

name: David captures Jerusalem from the Jebusites
note: David captures the Jebusite fortress in Jerusalem and establishes it as his royal city.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 93

name: Jerusalem becomes the City of David and royal capital
note: David establishes the conquered fortress as Ir David and the political center of the united monarchy.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 93

name: Uzzah dies during the first attempt to bring the Ark to Jerusalem
note: During the procession from Kiryat Ye'arim, Uzzah dies after touching the Ark; David temporarily stops the transfer.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 93

name: Ark remains three months with Oved Edom
note: The Ark is left with Oved Edom HaGiti for three months before the procession resumes.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 93

name: Ark is brought to Jerusalem
note: David completes the ceremonial transfer of the Ark into his new capital.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 93

name: David institutes the Jerusalem blessing in Birkat HaMazon in rabbinic tradition
note: David institutes the Jerusalem blessing in Birkat HaMazon in rabbinic tradition.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 93

name: Natan tells David that his son will build the Temple
note: The prophet Natan tells David that the permanent Temple will be built by his son rather than by David himself.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 93

name: David and Bat Sheva episode
note: The Bat Sheva episode is dated to 24 Elul and David's forgiveness to Yom Kippur.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 93

name: Shlomo is born
note: Shlomo is born.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 94

name: Amnon assaults Tamar
note: The Amnon and Tamar episode is placed in the following year.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 94

name: Avshalom kills Amnon and flees to Geshur
note: Avshalom takes revenge for Tamar and flees from David's court to Geshur.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 94

name: Avshalom declares himself king in Hebron
note: After returning to Jerusalem, Avshalom launches a rebellion and declares himself king with support from Achitofel.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 94

name: Avshalom is killed and his rebellion collapses
note: Avshalom is caught during the fighting and killed by Yoav and his men.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 94

name: Sheva ben Bichri launches another rebellion against David
note: After Avshalom's defeat, Sheva ben Bichri leads another rebellion and is ultimately killed.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 94

name: David orders a census of fighting-age men
note: A census of 1.3 million draftable men and extrapolates a population of more than five million.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 94

name: Adoniyahu proclaims himself king
note: Near David's death, Adoniyahu attempts to seize the succession with support from Yoav.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 94

name: Natan and Bat Sheva secure Shlomo's succession
note: Natan advises Bat Sheva to remind David of his promise that Shlomo should inherit the throne.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 94

name: Shlomo is publicly anointed king
note: David sends Tzadok, Natan and Benayahu to publicly anoint the young Shlomo; Adoniyahu's support dissolves.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 94

name: David dies in Jerusalem
note: David's death is placed in Ir David on Shavuot.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 94

name: Codex attributes Tehillim to David and earlier elders
note: Tehillim is attributed to David and earlier elders.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 94

name: Construction of the First Temple begins
note: Shlomo begins building the Beit Hamikdash in Iyar using preparations made by David.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 94

name: Hiram of Tyre supplies cedar and craftsmen for the Temple
note: The Phoenician alliance provides cedar from Lebanon and specialist builders for the Jerusalem Temple.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 94

name: Mishkan components are hidden beneath the Temple in rabbinic tradition
note: Mishkan components are hidden beneath the Temple in rabbinic tradition.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 94

name: Shlomo adds to the third blessing of Birkat HaMazon in rabbinic tradition
note: Shlomo expanded the blessing associated with Jerusalem and the Temple.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 94

name: First Temple construction is completed
note: Completion of the First Beit Hamikdash after seven years of construction.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 94

name: Ark is installed in the First Temple
note: Shlomo gathers the people and brings the Ark into the completed Temple.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 94

name: National dedication celebrations accompany the Temple opening
note: A seven-day celebration before Sukkot, including sacrificial festivities during Yom Kippur.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 94

name: Final finishing work on the Temple is completed in Cheshvan
note: The final building details are completed after the dedication.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 94

name: Shlomo has Shimi executed
note: Shlomo finding grounds to execute Shimi, who had cursed David during Avshalom's rebellion.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 94

name: Shlomo marries Pharaoh's daughter
note: Shlomo's marriage into the Egyptian royal house becomes part of his international political network.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 94

name: Shlomo and Hiram exchange royal gifts and cities
note: Hiram supplies silver and timber, and the rulers exchange gifts including cities.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 94

name: Shlomo dies
note: Shlomo dies after a long reign and the united monarchy enters a succession crisis.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 94

name: Codex attributes Mishlei, Kohelet and Shir HaShirim to Shlomo
note: Mishlei, Kohelet and Shir HaShirim is attributed to Shlomo.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 94

name: Achiyah prophesies that Yerav'am will rule ten tribes
note: Achiyah HaShiloni predicts the division of the kingdom and Yerav'am's northern rule.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 96

name: Rechav'am succeeds Shlomo in Judah
note: Rechav'am rejects the elders' advice and promises a harsher rule.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 96

name: Northern tribes reject Rechav'am
note: The northern tribes reject Rechav'am's rule after his refusal to reduce the burdens imposed under Shlomo.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 96

name: Yerav'am I becomes king of the northern Kingdom of Israel
note: The northern tribes choose Yerav'am ben Nevat as king.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 96

name: United monarchy divides into Israel and Judah
note: The kingdom permanently divides into the northern Kingdom of Israel and the southern Kingdom of Judah.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 96

name: Yerav'am establishes cult centers with golden calves at Bethel and Dan
note: Yerav'am creates northern cult centers at Bethel and Dan to reduce dependence on Jerusalem.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 96

name: Yerav'am posts guards to restrict pilgrimage to Jerusalem
note: Guards are stationed to prevent northern subjects travelling to the Jerusalem Temple.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 96

name: Shishak of Egypt raids Jerusalem
note: Egyptian forces invade and remove treasures from the Temple and royal palace.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 96

name: Aviyah succeeds Rechav'am as king of Judah
note: Aviyah/Avijam becomes king and repeatedly fights Yerav'am I.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 96

name: Judah and Israel fight under Aviyah and Yerav'am
note: Persistent war continues between the divided kingdoms.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 96

name: Assa succeeds Aviyah as king of Judah
note: Assa succeeds Aviyah as king of Judah.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 96

name: Judah enjoys an initial decade of peace under Assa
note: The first ten years of Assa's reign as peaceful.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 96

name: Ido confronts Yerav'am and is later killed by a lion
note: The prophet Ido criticizes Yerav'am's cultic policies and later dies in the lion episode.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 96

name: Achiyah foretells the end of Yerav'am's dynasty
note: Yerav'am's wife secretly consults Achiyah about their sick son, and the prophet predicts the dynasty's fall.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 96

name: Nadav succeeds Yerav'am I as king of Israel
note: Yerav'am's son Nadav takes the northern throne.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 96

name: Baasha assassinates Nadav
note: Baasha ben Achiyah kills Nadav and destroys Yerav'am's royal family.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 96

name: Baasha becomes king of Israel
note: Baasha establishes a new northern dynasty while retaining Yerav'am's cultic system.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 96

name: Baasha and Assa go to war
note: The northern and southern kingdoms resume direct warfare.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 96

name: Zerach HaKushi invades Judah and is defeated by Assa
note: A vast invading army under Zerach being defeated by Assa.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 96

name: Elah succeeds Baasha as king of Israel
note: Elah becomes king of the northern kingdom.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 96

name: Yehu ben Chanani prophesies the end of Baasha's dynasty
note: The prophet warns that the dynasty will fall because it follows Yerav'am's path.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 96

name: Zimri assassinates Elah and his family
note: The palace officer Zimri kills Elah and the royal household and declares himself king.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 96

name: Army proclaims Omri king
note: The army responds to Zimri's coup by proclaiming its general Omri king.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 97

name: Zimri dies after a seven-day reign
note: Trapped by Omri's forces, Zimri burns the palace and dies.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 97

name: Tivni challenges Omri for the northern throne
note: A prolonged factional struggle continues between supporters of Omri and Tivni.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 97

name: Tivni is killed and Omri gains undisputed rule
note: After several years of civil conflict, Omri becomes sole king of Israel.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 97

name: Omri establishes Samaria as capital of Israel
note: Omri builds up Shomron/Samaria as the northern kingdom's capital.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 97

name: Achav succeeds Omri as king of Israel
note: Achav becomes king and, with Izevel, strongly promotes Baal worship.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 97

name: Achav and Izevel persecute prophets
note: An attempt to kill the prophets opposed to the royal religious program.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 97

name: Eliyahu confronts the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel
note: Eliyahu publicly challenges the Baal cult during the drought and defeats its prophets in the biblical account.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 97

name: Izevel seeks Eliyahu's death
note: After the Carmel confrontation, Izevel threatens Eliyahu and he flees.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 97

name: Ovadya hides and supports one hundred prophets
note: Ovadya shelters persecuted prophets in caves and spends his wealth supporting them.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 97

name: Assa dies and Yehoshaphat becomes king of Judah
note: Assa dies and Yehoshaphat becomes king of Judah.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 97

name: Yehoshaphat sends teachers throughout Judah
note: Yehoshaphat sends officials and teachers, including Ovadya and Michiyahu, through Judah to teach the people.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 97

name: Achav repents after the Navot vineyard episode
note: Achav repents after the Navot vineyard episode.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 97

name: Achav is killed in battle against Aram
note: After a three-year pause in war, Achav is mortally wounded in battle, as Michiyahu had predicted.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 97

name: Achazyahu I succeeds Achav as king of Israel
note: Achav's son Achazyahu becomes king.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 97

name: Eliyahu ascends in a chariot of fire

source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 97

name: Elisha succeeds Eliyahu as leading prophet
note: Elisha remains as the principal prophetic figure after Eliyahu's departure.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 97

name: Achazyahu I dies after his fall
note: Achazyahu dies after a serious fall from an upper room.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 97

name: Yehoram I becomes king of Israel
note: Because Achazyahu has no son, his brother Yehoram succeeds him.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 97

name: Yehoram II becomes king of Judah
note: Yehoram begins ruling Judah before the death of his father Yehoshaphat.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 97

name: Yehoram II's marriage to Athalya links Judah to Achav's dynasty
note: The marriage creates a close dynastic connection between Judah and the Omride house.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 97

name: Yehoram II turns toward Omride religious policies
note: His rule deteriorates as he follows the model of Achav's house.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 97

name: Achazyahu II becomes king of Judah
note: Achazyahu II succeeds during his father Yehoram II's final illness.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 97

name: Yehu is designated for kingship by Elisha's prophetic circle
note: Elisha's messenger anoints or designates Yehu to overthrow the Omride dynasty.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 97

name: Yehu rebels against Yehoram I
note: Yehu launches a coup against the northern king.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 97

name: Yehu kills Yehoram I king of Israel
note: The coup kills the reigning northern monarch.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 97

name: Izevel is killed during Yehu's coup
note: Izevel is killed as Yehu destroys the remaining Omride royal house.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 97

name: Yehu becomes king of Israel
note: Yehu establishes a new dynasty after eliminating the house of Achav.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 97

name: Yehu destroys organized Baal worship of Achav's dynasty
note: Yehu uses deception to gather and eliminate Baal worshippers and destroys the royal Baal cult.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 97

name: Yehu kills Achazyahu II king of Judah
note: The northern coup also kills the king of Judah.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 98

name: Athalya seizes the throne of Judah

source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 98

name: Yehosheva rescues the infant Yeho'ash
note: Yehosheva saves her nephew from Athalya's purge.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 98

name: Yeho'ash is hidden in the Temple for six years
note: The surviving Davidic heir is concealed in the Temple under protection of Yehoyada.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 98

name: Yehoyada crowns Yeho'ash I king of Judah
note: After six years in hiding, the young Yeho'ash is publicly installed as king.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 98

name: Athalya is killed and Davidic rule is restored
note: The coup led by Yehoyada ends Athalya's rule and restores the Davidic dynasty.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 98

name: Yeho'achaz I succeeds Yehu as king of Israel
note: Yehu's son takes the northern throne.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 98

name: Yona prophesies four generations for Yehu's dynasty
note: Yona is associated with the prophecy that Yehu's dynasty would continue for four generations.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 98

name: Aram dominates Israel under Yeho'achaz I
note: The kingdom of Israel is heavily pressured by Chazael and Ben-Hadad II of Aram.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 98

name: Yeho'ash I renovates the First Temple
note: Yeho'ash I renovates the First Temple.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 98

name: Yeho'ash II becomes king of Israel
note: Yeho'ash II succeeds his father Yeho'achaz.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 98

name: Elisha dies
note: The death of the prophet Elisha.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 98

name: Yehoyada Kohen Gadol dies
note: The high priest who protected and installed Yeho'ash I dies.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 98

name: Yeho'ash I abandons Yehoyada's religious guidance
note: Yeho'ash I abandons Yehoyada's religious guidance.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 98

name: Zecharyah ben Yehoyada is killed in the Temple court
note: Yeho'ash I orders the killing of the high priest Zecharyah on Yom Kippur.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 98

name: Yeho'ash I is assassinated
note: The king is killed in bed by his servants after the killing of Zecharyah.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 98

name: Amatzya becomes king of Judah
note: Amatzya succeeds his father Yeho'ash I.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 98

name: Amatzya defeats Edom

note: Mattityahu launches the Hasmonean revolt at Modi'in.

name: Egyptian Jewish pilgrims and artisans contribute skills at the Temple
note: Jews from Egypt visit for festivals and Egyptian artisans contribute specialist Temple skills.

name: Yonatan is killed and Shimon succeeds him
note: Yonatan is killed and his brother Shimon becomes ruler.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 126

name: Shimon the Hasmonean is assassinated
note: Shimon the Hasmonean is assassinated.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 126

name: Two older sons of Shimon are killed in the assassination plot
note: Two of Shimon's older sons are also killed.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 126

name: John Hyrcanus I escapes and becomes ruler
note: Yochanan Hyrcanus escapes the plot and succeeds his father.

note: Campaigns north and south that greatly expand Hasmonean territory.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 126

name: Codex says Hyrcanus opens King David's tomb to obtain funds

name: Roman influence becomes stronger in Hasmonean diplomacy
note: Rome takes a more dominant position in its relationship with Judaea.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 126

name: Hyrcanus's conquests bring a period of peace and prosperity
note: The enlarged kingdom as relatively peaceful and prosperous.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 126

name: John Hyrcanus captures Shechem
note: Hasmonean forces capture the principal Samaritan center.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 126

name: John Hyrcanus destroys the Samaritan temple on Mount Gerizim

source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 126

name: Banquet dispute turns John Hyrcanus against the Pharisees

name: John Hyrcanus persecutes Pharisaic scholarly leaders

note: The scholar Yehoshua ben Perachya escapes persecution by fleeing to Egypt.

name: Shimon ben Shatach is hidden by his sister Salome
note: Shimon ben Shatach survives the persecution because his sister conceals him.

name: John Hyrcanus I dies
note: Hyrcanus dies after a long reign of territorial expansion and religious-political conflict.

name: Judah Aristobulus succeeds John Hyrcanus I
note: Judah Aristobulus succeeds John Hyrcanus I.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 126

name: Codex says Aristobulus commercializes the high priestly office

source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 126

name: Aristobulus imprisons Alexander Jannaeus
note: Aristobulus imprisons his brother Alexander Yannai.

name: Aristobulus imprisons his mother, who dies in confinement
note: His mother dies while imprisoned.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 126

name: Aristobulus kills his brother Antigonus
note: Aristobulus kills his favored younger brother after suspecting a revolt.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 126

name: Aristobulus I dies without children
note: The sick Aristobulus dies shortly after the killing of Antigonus.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 127

name: Alexander Jannaeus is released and succeeds as ruler
note: Alexander Yannai is released from prison and becomes Hasmonean ruler.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 127

name: Salome Alexandra becomes wife and political partner of Alexander Jannaeus

name: Shimon ben Shatach enters the Sanhedrin
note: Shimon ben Shatach enters the Sanhedrin.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 127

name: Shimon ben Shatach gradually replaces Sadducean Sanhedrin members
note: Shimon uses scholarship and strategy to replace Sadducean members with his disciples.

name: Codex places a Yeshua ben Sitda disciplinary episode in this period
note: A student called Yeshua ben Sitda being rejected for misconduct and later punished by a Sanhedrin.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 127

name: Codex places Yehoshua ben Gamla's high-priestly appointment under Alexander Jannaeus

name: Codex associates Yehoshua ben Gamla with a national Torah school system

name: Shimon ben Shatach calls Yehoshua ben Perachya back from Egypt
note: Shimon secretly asks his mentor to return from exile.

name: Alexander Jannaeus contributes to sacrifices of poorer Jews
note: Shimon ben Shatach persuades the king to help fund sacrifices for poorer worshippers.

name: Alexander Jannaeus appears before the Sanhedrin over a murder allegation involving his servant
note: A confrontation between royal power and the Sanhedrin.

name: Royal court confrontation contributes to a rule limiting kings in judicial proceedings
note: Royal court confrontation contributes to a rule limiting kings in judicial proceedings.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 128

name: Alexander Jannaeus persecutes Pharisaic scholars
note: Alexander Jannaeus persecutes Pharisaic scholars.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 128

name: Choni HaMe'agel remains a prominent sage
note: Choni HaMe'agel surviving and remaining influential during the conflict.

name: Popular rebellion against Alexander Jannaeus becomes a prolonged civil war
note: Open warfare against Jannaeus lasts six years.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 128

name: Codex reports at least fifty thousand deaths in Jannaeus's civil war
note: A toll of at least 50,000 deaths.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 128

name: Alexander Jannaeus executes eight hundred opponents and their families
note: The notorious mass killing of roughly 800 opponents and violence against their families.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 128

name: Alexander Jannaeus expresses regret near death
note: Jannaeus expresses regret and advises Salome to cooperate with the Pharisees.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 128

name: Salome Alexandra succeeds Alexander Jannaeus
note: Salome Alexandra becomes ruler of the Hasmonean kingdom.

name: Salome Alexandra restores cooperation with the Pharisees
note: Pharisaic leaders regain strong influence in government and law.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 128

name: Hyrcanus II receives authority over Temple affairs
note: Salome places her son Hyrcanus II over Temple-related matters.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 128

name: Aristobulus II serves as a regional governor
note: Salome's younger son Aristobulus is placed in regional authority away from Jerusalem.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 128

name: Yehoshua ben Perachya and Nitai HaArbeli have died by Salome's reign
note: The passing of the previous Sanhedrin leadership.

name: Yehuda ben Tabbai returns from Egypt

source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 128

name: Shimon ben Shatach and Yehuda ben Tabbai lead the Sanhedrin
note: Them as the Nasi and Av during Salome's reign.

name: Sadducees regain political influence under Aristobulus II

note: Antipater encourages Hyrcanus to challenge Aristobulus again.

note: Pompey places the weaker Hyrcanus II in power with Antipater as his minister.

note: The Roman-backed administration permits Torah scholarship to flourish again.

name: Shemaya and Avtalyon have died by this point

note: The revolt is defeated with Roman assistance.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 129

source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 129

name: Shammai establishes his own Beit Midrash
note: Shammai opens an independent school of study.

name: Admon and Chanan become renowned judges
note: Admon and Chanan become renowned judges.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 129

note: Public pressure forces Hyrcanus II to summon the young Herod for trial.

name: Herod appears before the court with armed supporters
note: Herod appears in a threatening manner with armed men.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 129

name: Shammai challenges Herod before the court
note: Shammai is credited with insisting that the proceedings continue despite intimidation.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 129

name: Hyrcanus II postpones Herod's trial and Herod escapes
note: The trial is postponed and Herod avoids judgment.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 129

name: Antigonus Mattathias gains Parthian support
note: Antigonus, son of Aristobulus II, secures Parthian military backing against the Roman-supported Hyrcanus II.

name: Parthian-backed forces capture Jerusalem for Antigonus
note: Antigonus and his Parthian allies seize Jerusalem and displace Hyrcanus II.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 129

name: Antigonus becomes the final Hasmonean ruler
note: Mattathias Antigonus becomes king and high priest in the last restoration of direct Hasmonean rule.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 129

name: Hyrcanus II is captured and taken into the Parthian realm
note: Hyrcanus is taken east after Antigonus's takeover.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 129

name: Hyrcanus II is mutilated and rendered ineligible for the high priesthood
note: External sources record that Antigonus had Hyrcanus's ears mutilated so he could not serve as high priest.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 129

name: Codex says Hyrcanus II later leads Jews in the eastern diaspora
note: Hyrcanus was later released and became a leader among Jews living in the Parthian kingdom, including Babylonia.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 129

name: Hasmonean rule enters its final phase under Antigonus
note: Antigonus's restoration lasts until Herod's Roman-backed conquest, which is assigned to the next Roman/Herodian file.

name: Herod I takes control of Judaea with Roman military support

name: Herod consolidates his rule through severe repression
note: The first years of Herod’s rule as a period in which intimidation and violence were used to compel acceptance of the new regime.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 130

name: Herod expands fortresses including Masada
note: Herod strengthened strategic fortresses, including Masada, as part of a broad program of royal consolidation and monumental construction.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 130

name: Herod develops Hellenistic-Roman cities with large non-Jewish populations
note: Herod’s construction and settlement policy in cities whose civic culture differed sharply from Jerusalem’s Jewish religious character.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 130

name: Caesarea becomes a major Herodian royal and port city
note: The completion of Caesarea and a major royal celebration, presenting the city as a possible alternative center of royal power to Jerusalem.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 130

name: Hillel comes from Babylonia to Jerusalem for Passover
note: Hillel returned from Babylonia and, according to rabbinic tradition, resolved a difficult Passover-law question that the Bene Bathyra leadership could not answer.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 130

name: Bene Bathyra step aside and Hillel becomes leading Torah authority
note: The Bene Bathyra voluntarily yielded leadership after Hillel demonstrated superior knowledge of the relevant halakhic tradition.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 130

name: Tradition places Hillel as Nasi with Shammai as Av Bet Din
note: Tradition places Hillel as Nasi with Shammai as Av Bet Din.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 130

name: Hillel opens a separate Beit Midrash from Shammai
note: Hillel and Shammai operating separate schools rather than a single combined study institution.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 130

name: Codex marks the beginning of the Tannaitic era under Hillel
note: The beginning of the Tannaitic era under Hillel.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 130

name: Herod begins rebuilding and enlarging the Second Temple
note: Herod launched a vast reconstruction of the Temple complex, enlarging the sacred platform and rebuilding the sanctuary and courts on a monumental scale.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 130

name: Bava ben Buta is associated by tradition with encouraging the Temple project
note: Bava ben Buta is associated by tradition with encouraging the Temple project.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 130

name: Codex marks completion of the major Herodian Temple renovation
note: Completion of the principal renovation is dated to 11 BCE and describes the Temple as exceptionally magnificent.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 130

name: Golden eagle is placed above an entrance to the Temple
note: A Roman imperial eagle above the Temple entrance, later becoming the focus of resistance by religious scholars and students.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 130

name: Religious students tear down Herod’s golden eagle
note: After a rumor that Herod had died, religious scholars and students pulled down the royal golden eagle from the Temple entrance.

name: Herod executes participants in the golden-eagle protest
note: Herod executes participants in the golden-eagle protest.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 132

name: Herod orders mass detention shortly before his death
note: Herod ordered one person from each Jewish family arrested, intending that they be killed when he died so that the country would mourn.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 132

name: Herod appoints Archelaus as his intended successor
note: Near the end of his life Herod designated his son Archelaus to rule Judaea, subject to Roman imperial approval.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 132

name: Herod I dies
note: Herod’s death is dated to 2 Shevat and notes that Salome initially concealed it until detained Jews could be released.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 132

name: Salome releases prisoners whom Herod had ordered killed
note: Before publicly announcing Herod’s death, Salome arranged for the recently detained Jews to be released.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 132

name: Archelaus succeeds Herod in Judaea pending Roman approval
note: Archelaus assumed authority after Herod’s death but still required confirmation from Augustus.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 132

name: Archelaus suppresses Passover unrest with a massacre
note: Archelaus forcibly halted the Passover sacrifice and that thousands were killed in the crackdown.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 132

name: Jewish delegation appeals to Augustus against Herodian kingship
note: A Jewish delegation, joined by Jews in Rome, asked Augustus not to confirm a new Herodian king.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 132

name: Augustus confirms Archelaus only as ethnarch rather than king
note: Archelaus prevailed in Rome sufficiently to receive rule over Judaea and related territories, but not the full title of king.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 132

name: Roman Syrian forces intervene in Judaea during Archelaus’s absence
note: Roman forces from Syria entered Judaea amid reports of unrest while Archelaus was in Rome.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 132

name: Roman troops extort Jewish communities during the intervention
note: Abusive extortion by a Roman commander’s household troops, provoking widespread protest and eventual recall.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 132

name: Hillel dies
note: Hillel died after reshaping the rabbinic leadership and establishing a school whose traditions became central to later Judaism.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 132

name: Shimon son of Hillel succeeds as leader of the Sanhedrin
note: Hillel was succeeded by his son Shimon in the elevated leadership office.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 132

name: Rabban Gamliel I succeeds Shimon
note: After Shimon’s short tenure, his son Gamliel I became a leading figure of the Sanhedrin and the first in the dynasty widely styled Rabban.
