name: Saadia Gaon writes extensively and confronts Karaite claims
note: Saadia Gaon authored many works, including Emunot VeDeyot and piyyutim, and was actively engaged in rebutting Karaite arguments, which were influential in Eretz Yisrael.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 174

name: Forced conversions and massacre of Jews in Italy
note: Forced conversions in parts of Italy and a massacre of Jews in Bari. It also records a tradition that Chisdai ibn Shaprut secured withdrawal of an expulsion order.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 174

name: R. Tzemach III becomes Gaon of Pumbedita
note: R. Tzemach III became Gaon of Pumbedita, succeeding R. Kohen Tzedek II.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 174

name: R. Chanina VII becomes Gaon of Pumbedita
note: R. Chanina VII becomes Gaon of Pumbedita.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 174

name: R. Aharon becomes Gaon of Pumbedita
note: R. Aharon became Gaon of Pumbedita, succeeding R. Chanina VII.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 174

name: A new ruling dynasty begins a century of persecution in Bavel
note: A new “fanatic” dynasty took control of Bavel and that Jews suffered persecution during roughly a century of its rule.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 174

name: The “Four Captives” are ransomed into new centres of Torah learning
note: The “Four Captives” are ransomed into new centres of Torah learning.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 175

name: R. Dunash ben Labrat challenges Menachem’s Hebrew dictionary
note: R. Dunash ben Labrat of Baghdad, a disciple of Saadia Gaon, developed a grammatical critique of Menachem ben Saruk’s dictionary and also composed poetry and piyyutim.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 175

name: R. Menachem ben Saruk composes the Machberet
note: R. Menachem ben Saruk composes the Machberet.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 175

name: R. Nechemyah becomes Gaon of Pumbedita
note: R. Nechemyah becomes Gaon of Pumbedita.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 175

name: R. Sherira Gaon becomes Gaon of Pumbedita
note: R. Sherira Gaon became Gaon of Pumbedita, succeeding R. Nechemyah.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 175

name: R. Hai III becomes the last Gaon of Pumbedita
note: R. Sherira stepped aside according to some accounts and his son R. Hai Gaon (Hai III) succeeded him as Gaon of Pumbedita, becoming the last Gaon of the academy.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 175

name: R. Sherira Gaon writes his historical Iggeret
note: R. Sherira Gaon writes his historical Iggeret.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 175

name: Sherira and Hai are arrested after denunciation to the caliph
note: Sherira and Hai are arrested after denunciation to the caliph.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 175

name: Forced conversions and synagogue burnings in Eretz Yisrael; Jews marked in Egypt
note: Forced conversion of some Jews under Muslim rulers in Eretz Yisrael, the burning of synagogues, and a requirement that Jews in Egypt wear a distinctive sign on their clothing.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 175

name: Anti-Jewish riots and forced conversions spread through France
note: Anti-Jewish riots and forced conversions spread through France.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 175

name: Mainz conversion-or-expulsion decree (withdrawn within the year)
note: Mainz conversion-or-expulsion decree (withdrawn within the year).
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 176

name: R. Shimon HaGadol serves on the Mainz Beit Din and composes piyyutim
note: R. Shimon HaGadol ben Yitzchak is placed in Mainz at this time, serving on the city’s Beit Din with Rabbenu Gershom Me’or HaGola and composing piyyutim that entered the High Holy Day liturgy.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 176

name: The R. Amnon and Unetaneh Tokef tradition is placed in Mainz
note: The tradition of R. Amnon of Mainz: after asking for time to consider conversion, he was mutilated for refusing Christianity and was brought to the synagogue on Rosh Hashanah, where he is said to have composed Unetaneh Tokef before dying.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 176

name: R. Eliyahu ben Shemayahu of Bari is active as a paytan
note: Another paytan of this period, R. Eliyahu ben Shemayahu of Bari in southern Italy.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 176

name: R. Yekutiel of Speyer contributes piyyutim to the Machzor
note: R. Yekutiel ben Moshe of the Klonymos family in Speyer is noted as a paytan whose compositions became prominent in the High Holy Day Machzor.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 176

name: R. Shlomo ben Yehuda HaBavli’s piyyut legacy is noted
note: The paytan R. Shlomo ben Yehuda HaBavli had died approximately twenty-five years earlier, placing his liturgical-poetic legacy in the background of the Mainz-era discussion.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 176

name: Berber conquest of Córdoba brings Jewish deaths and political fragmentation
note: Many Jews were killed when Berber forces from North Africa conquered Córdoba and Spain fractured into multiple political units.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 176

name: R. Shmuel HaNagid flees Córdoba for Granada
note: Following the upheaval in Córdoba, R. Shmuel HaNagid fled to Granada, where he later became highly influential.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 176

name: R. Chanoch of Córdoba dies after a synagogue accident
note: R. Chanoch of Córdoba dies after a synagogue accident.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 176

name: Six thousand Jews massacred in Fez
note: Approximately 6,000 Jews were massacred in Fez, Morocco, at around this time, possibly in connection with an invasion.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 176

name: R. Hai Gaon dies and the Babylonian academies rapidly decline
note: R. Hai Gaon dies and the Babylonian academies rapidly decline.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 176

name: R. Chizkiyah succeeds R. Hai and is killed two years later
note: R. Hai was succeeded by R. Chizkiyah, a grandson of David ben Zakkai, and that R. Chizkiyah was killed two years later.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 176

name: Rabbenu Gershom Me’or HaGolah dies in Mainz
note: Rabbenu Gershom Me’or HaGolah dies in Mainz.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 185

name: R. Chizkiyah Gaon is arrested, tortured and killed
note: R. Chizkiyah Gaon, connected with the final phase of the Babylonian Geonate, was denounced to the ruler, arrested, tortured and killed.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 185

name: Rabbenu Nissim Gaon dies in Kairouan
note: Rabbenu Nissim Gaon died in Kairouan, one of the leading North African Torah centres that inherited elements of the Geonic scholarly tradition.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 185

name: Rabbenu Chananel dies in Kairouan
note: Rabbenu Chananel's death shortly after that of Rabbenu Nissim is placed around 1050, while noting an alternative tradition that places it roughly a decade earlier.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 185

name: R. Shmuel HaNagid dies in Granada
note: R. Shmuel HaNagid, a leading Talmud scholar, poet and statesman in Muslim Spain, died in Granada.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 185

name: R. Yosef HaNagid succeeds his father in Granada
note: Following the death of R. Shmuel HaNagid, his son R. Yosef HaNagid succeeded him in Granada.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 185

name: R. Shlomo ibn Gabirol composes ethical and liturgical works in Spain
note: R. Shlomo ibn Gabirol's literary activity is placed around this period, including Tikkun Middot HaNefesh and major Hebrew poetry.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 185

name: R. Meir ben Yitzchak composes major piyyutim including Akdamot
note: Around this period R. Meir ben Yitzchak, a scholar cited by Rashi, was active in Germany and composed liturgical poetry including Akdamot.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 185

name: R. Yosef HaNagid is killed in Granada
note: R. Yosef HaNagid was killed at the gates of Granada on Shabbat, 9 Tevet 1066.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 185

name: Granada massacre devastates the Jewish community
note: About 4,000 Jews were killed in the violence following R. Yosef HaNagid's death and that Granada's influential Jewish community temporarily ceased to function.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 185

name: The Rif flees Morocco and arrives in Spain
note: R. Yitzchak Alfasi (the Rif) fled Morocco after being denounced, reached Spain and soon became rabbi of the largely Jewish town of Lucena.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 185

name: Pope Urban II’s crusade call sets the First Crusade in motion
note: The 1096 persecutions in the context of Urban II's call for a crusade to Jerusalem; crusading bands attacked Jewish communities before leaving Europe.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 185

name: Jews of Speyer are attacked during the First Crusade
note: Jews of Speyer are attacked during the First Crusade.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 185

name: First Crusade attackers massacre Jews in Worms
note: Crusaders attacked the Jewish community of Worms in Iyar 1096. Many were killed and others sought refuge with the bishop.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 185

name: Refugees in the bishop’s stronghold at Worms are massacred
note: Jews who had taken refuge in the bishop's stronghold at Worms were killed on Rosh Chodesh Sivan while Hallel was being recited.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 186

name: R. Klonymos of Rome is killed at Worms
note: R. Klonymos of Rome, a successor to R. Yaakov ben Yakar in Worms, was killed in the 1096 persecutions.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 186

name: Simcha ben Yitzchak HaKohen is killed during a forced-baptism episode
note: Simcha ben Yitzchak HaKohen stabbed the bishop's nephew while being subjected to forced baptism and was then killed.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 186

name: Jews of Neuss are massacred during the First Crusade
note: Crusading violence reached Neuss in early Sivan 1096 and the Jewish community was massacred.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 186

name: Mainz Jewish community is massacred
note: Roughly 1,000 Jews of Mainz were massacred on 3 Sivan during the Rhineland persecutions.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 186

name: Jews of Bacharach are massacred before Shavuot
note: The Jewish community of Bacharach was massacred on the eve of Shavuot during the First Crusade persecutions.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 186

name: Jews in Cologne face forced baptism and martyrdom
note: Jews in Cologne face forced baptism and martyrdom.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 186

name: Jews at Xanten die rather than submit to forced baptism
note: A group of Jews at Xanten taking their own lives on 5 Tammuz rather than be massacred or forced to convert.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 186

name: Jews of Mehr are massacred
note: A massacre of Jews in a place rendered 'Mehr' in Germany on 6 Tammuz during the 1096 wave of attacks.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 186

name: Cologne Jews are attacked again in Tammuz
note: Cologne Jews are attacked again in Tammuz.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 186

name: Crusaders attack Jews in Troyes
note: Troyes among the additional Jewish communities attacked by crusading bands during the 1096 persecutions.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 186

name: Crusaders attack Jews in Metz
note: Metz among the additional Jewish communities attacked by crusading bands during the 1096 persecutions.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 186

name: Crusaders attack Jews in Regensburg
note: Regensburg among the additional Jewish communities attacked by crusading bands during the 1096 persecutions.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 186

name: Crusaders attack Jews in Prague
note: Prague among the additional Jewish communities attacked by crusading bands during the 1096 persecutions.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 186

name: Crusaders attack Jews in Pressburg
note: Pressburg among the additional Jewish communities attacked by crusading bands during the 1096 persecutions.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 186

name: Ashkenazi refugees move east toward Poland-Lithuania
note: Substantial eastward migration of German Jews after the Crusade persecutions; the migrants carried the language culture that later developed into Yiddish. The migration was a process extending beyond a single year, but the JSON anchors it to 1096 to avoid a permanently displayed map label.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 186

name: Henry IV permits forcibly baptized Jews to return openly to Judaism
note: Jews who had been forcibly baptized during the 1096 persecutions were permitted by Emperor Henry IV to return openly to Judaism one year later.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 186

name: Crusaders capture Jerusalem
note: After a siege, First Crusade forces captured Jerusalem in 1099 and established the Latin Kingdom of Jerusalem.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 186

name: Jerusalem’s Jews are killed in a synagogue fire after the Crusader conquest
note: Jews were forced into a synagogue which the Crusaders burned, killing almost all those inside; Jews were then barred from living in the new Crusader kingdom's capital.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 186

name: The Rif dies in Lucena
note: R. Yitzchak Alfasi (the Rif) died in Lucena. His halachic digest became one of the foundational works of the Rishonim.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 186

name: The Ri Migash succeeds the Rif in Lucena
note: R. Yosef HaLevi ibn Migash, a young disciple of the Rif, succeeded him in leadership at Lucena.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 186

name: Sefer HeAruch is completed in Rome
note: A tradition that the Ba'al HaAruch completed Sefer HeAruch about a year before his death.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 187

name: Rashi dies in Troyes
note: Rashi died in Troyes on 29 Tammuz. His biblical and Talmudic commentaries became foundational to later Jewish learning.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 186

name: The Tosafist era begins
note: Rashi's death as the opening of the Tosafist era, in which his descendants and later scholars developed the dialectical Tosafot tradition. The event is intentionally stored as a single-year transition marker so it does not remain permanently visible on the map.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 186

name: R. Simcha, compiler of Machzor Vitry, dies
note: Rashi's disciple R. Simcha, associated with the compilation of Machzor Vitry, died in the same year as Rashi.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 186

name: R. Yehuda HaLevi composes or edits the Kuzari around this period
note: The composition or editing of the Kuzari by R. Yehuda HaLevi is placed around this time.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 186

name: R. Natan ben Yechiel, Ba’al HaAruch, dies in Rome
note: R. Natan ben Yechiel died in Rome after composing Sefer HeAruch, a major Aramaic-Hebrew lexicon of Talmudic terminology.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 187

name: Jews are expelled from Ghent and Flanders
note: The expulsion of Jews from Ghent and the wider province of Flanders.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 187

name: R. Baruch ben Yitzchak I dies
note: R. Baruch ben Yitzchak I dies.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 187

name: The Rambam (Maimonides) is born in Córdoba
note: R. Moshe ben Maimon, later known as the Rambam or Maimonides, was born in Córdoba in 1135.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 187

name: The Ri Migash dies
note: R. Yosef HaLevi ibn Migash died in 1141 after leading the Lucena scholarly centre.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 187

name: The William of Norwich accusation becomes the first recorded medieval European blood libel
note: The William of Norwich accusation becomes the first recorded medieval European blood libel.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 187

name: R. Peter ben Yosef is killed in Austria
note: R. Peter ben Yosef is killed in Austria.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 187

name: Second Crusade violence targets Jewish communities
note: The Second Crusade generated a new wave of anti-Jewish violence in Europe before the armies departed for the eastern Mediterranean.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 187

name: Jews of Würzburg are massacred during Second Crusade violence
note: A massacre of the Würzburg Jewish community on 24 Adar amid the Second Crusade.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 187

name: Jews of Cologne are attacked during the Second Crusade
note: The Cologne Jewish community was attacked in Nissan 1147; many Jews escaped to mountains or fortified places.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 187

name: Jews of Bacharach are attacked before Shavuot
note: An attack on the Jewish community of Bacharach on 5 Sivan during the Second Crusade.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 187

name: Rabbenu Tam is captured and assaulted by Crusaders
note: Crusaders captured Rabbenu Tam at Ramerupt, ransacked his house and damaged his Torah scroll. He escaped the following day after suffering serious injuries.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 187

name: Anti-Jewish violence erupts in Córdoba under Almohad pressure
note: Attacks on Córdoba's Jews, destruction of synagogues and forced conversions after a radical Islamic movement took power.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 188

name: The Rambam’s family flees Córdoba
note: R. Maimon ben Yosef and his family, including the young Rambam, left Córdoba amid persecution and forced-conversion pressure.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 188

name: R. Yosef Kimchi leaves Córdoba and settles in Narbonne
note: R. Yosef Kimchi, father of the Radak, fled Córdoba and resettled in Narbonne.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 188

name: R. Yehuda ibn Tibbon leaves Córdoba and settles in Lunel
note: R. Yehuda ibn Tibbon fled Córdoba and settled in Lunel, helping establish the Hebrew translation tradition of Arabic Jewish works.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 188

name: R. Zerachyah HaLevi writes HaMa’or in Lunel
note: R. Zerachyah HaLevi, the Ba'al HaMa'or, was composing HaMa'or, his critical commentary on the Rif, in Lunel around 1150.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 188

name: R. Avraham ibn Ezra writes his Shabbat letter in London
note: Ibn Ezra writing a letter concerning Shabbat in London on 14 Tevet 1158.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 188

name: Rabbenu Bachya ibn Paquda composes Chovot HaLevavot
note: The Arabic composition of Chovot HaLevavot is dated to around 1161 in Spain, while noting that some place it earlier.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 188

name: R. Eliezer ben Natan composes Even HaEzer
note: Around this period R. Eliezer ben Natan (the Ravan) composed Even HaEzer, a halachic and customs work.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 188

name: R. Eliezer of Metz composes Sefer Yere’im
note: R. Eliezer of Metz and his Sefer Yere'im is placed in this period.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 188

name: R. Avraham ibn Ezra dies
note: Ibn Ezra's death on Rosh Chodesh Adar 1164, while acknowledging alternative chronological traditions.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 188

name: The Rambam leaves Fez amid forced-conversion pressure
note: After several years in Fez, the Rambam and his family left Morocco as religious pressure intensified.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 188

name: The Rambam arrives at Acre
note: After a dangerous sea voyage, the Rambam reached Acre on 3 Sivan 1165.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 188

name: The Rambam visits Jerusalem
note: Several months after reaching Acre, the Rambam visited Jerusalem.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 188

name: The Rambam settles in Fustat, Egypt
note: After leaving Eretz Yisrael, the Rambam settled in Fustat, which became the centre of his communal, medical and literary activity.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 188

name: R. David ben Levi is killed in Worms
note: The killing of R. David ben Levi in Worms on 21 Cheshvan 1167.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 188

name: R. Yehuda ibn Tibbon translates major Judeo-Arabic works into Hebrew
note: A major phase of R. Yehuda ibn Tibbon's translation activity is placed around this time, including works associated with Saadia Gaon, Yehuda HaLevi, Ibn Gabirol and Rabbenu Bachya.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 188

name: Blood libel accusation occurs in Gloucester
note: A blood libel in Gloucester in 1168, part of the spread of ritual-murder accusations after Norwich.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 188

name: Blois blood-libel accusation leads to mass burning of Jews
note: Blois blood-libel accusation leads to mass burning of Jews.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 189

name: Rabbenu Tam dies
note: Rabbenu Tam dies.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 189

name: The Ra’avad III is briefly imprisoned on a false charge
note: R. Avraham ben David of Posquières was briefly imprisoned in Provence on a false charge.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 189

name: Benjamin of Tudela undertakes and records extensive travels
note: Benjamin of Tudela travelled widely through Jewish communities and recorded his observations in Sefer HaMasa'ot, an important witness to Jewish geography and communal life.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 189

name: R. Petachiah of Regensburg undertakes extensive travels
note: R. Petachiah of Regensburg travelled widely, with his journeys later recorded in a work commonly called Sivuv.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 189

name: The Rashbam dies
note: The death of the Rashbam is placed around 1174/1175.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 189

name: Ba’al HaIttur completes Sefer HaIttur
note: R. Yitzchak ben Abba Mari completed his encyclopedic halachic work Sefer HaIttur after roughly forty years of labour.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 189

name: Jews are seized in Paris during Shabbat services and held for ransom
note: Jews being seized while attending services in Paris on Shabbat and detained for ransom.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 189

name: Blood libel occurs in Bury St Edmunds
note: A blood-libel accusation at Bury St Edmunds in 1181.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 189

name: Blood libel occurs in Zaragoza
note: A blood-libel accusation in Zaragoza in 1182.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 189

name: Jews are expelled from part of France
note: An expulsion of Jews from part of France in 1182; later entries describe their return.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 189

name: R. Elchanan, son of the Ri, is killed in Dampierre
note: R. Elchanan, son and disciple of the Ri, was killed in Dampierre during his father's lifetime.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 189

name: Aaron of Lincoln dies and the Crown seizes his estate
note: After the death of the wealthy financier Aaron of Lincoln, Henry II seized his estate and created a royal administrative mechanism to collect the enormous outstanding debts.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 189

name: The Exchequer of Aaron develops into tighter royal control of Jewish lending
note: The handling of Aaron of Lincoln's debts as groundwork for debt registries that made Jewish lending more visible to the Crown and facilitated taxation.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 189

name: Saladin recaptures Jerusalem and Jews are permitted to return
note: After Saladin recaptured Jerusalem from the Crusader kingdom, Jews were again permitted to reside in the city.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 189

name: Anti-Jewish coronation riots erupt in London
note: Violence against Jews accompanied the coronation of Richard I in London.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 190

name: R. Yaakov of Orléans is killed in London
note: R. Yaakov of Orléans, a disciple of Rabbenu Tam, was killed with other Jews in the London coronation riots.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 190

name: Third-Crusade violence spreads across English Jewish communities
note: Crusading enthusiasm in England produced a wave of anti-Jewish violence in several towns in 1190.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 190

name: Jews of Norwich are massacred
note: A massacre of Norwich's Jewish community during the 1190 wave of violence.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 190

name: Jews are massacred at Stamford
note: A massacre of Jews at Stamford Fair in Adar 1190.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 190

name: York Jewish community is destroyed at Clifford’s Tower
note: The Jews of York, facing a besieging mob and demands for conversion, suffered mass death at the royal castle in March 1190.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 190

name: Fifty-seven Jews are killed at Bury St Edmunds
note: The killing of fifty-seven Jews in Bury St Edmunds on 9 Nissan 1190.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 190

name: One hundred Jews are burned in France by royal order
note: One hundred Jews being burned to death in France by order of the king.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 190

name: R. Shmuel ben Eli attempts to abolish the Exilarchate in Baghdad
note: R. Shmuel ben Eli, head of a reconstituted Baghdad yeshiva, unsuccessfully sought to abolish the position of Reish Galuta so communal funds could be redirected to the academy.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 190

name: The Radak composes his Tanakh commentary around this period
note: R. David Kimchi's composition of his biblical commentary is placed around 1191 in Narbonne.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 190

name: R. Yom Tov, disciple of Rabbenu Tam, is killed in York
note: The death in York of R. Yom Tov, a disciple of Rabbenu Tam and liturgical poet.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 190

name: R. Yaakov of Corbeil is killed
note: R. Yaakov of Corbeil, a disciple of Rabbenu Tam, was killed in 1192.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 190

name: Blood libel occurs in Winchester
note: A blood-libel accusation in Winchester in 1193.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 190

name: The Ramban (Nachmanides) is born in Girona
note: The Ramban (Nachmanides) is born in Girona.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 190

name: Third-Crusade participants massacre Jews in Vienna
note: The killing of fifteen Jews in Vienna by participants associated with the Third Crusade.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 190

name: R. Yitzchak ben Asher III is killed in Speyer
note: The killing in Speyer of R. Yitzchak ben Asher III, named for his grandfather the Riva.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 191

name: R. Shmuel ben Natrunai is tortured and killed with other Jews
note: R. Shmuel ben Natrunai is tortured and killed with other Jews.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 191

name: R. Elazar Roke’ach is wounded; his wife and children are killed
note: Attackers killed the wife and children of R. Elazar ben Yehuda Roke'ach in Worms and wounded him.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 191

name: Jews are permitted to return to previously expelled French areas
note: The readmission in 1198 of Jews to areas of France from which they had earlier been expelled.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 191

name: North African Jews are required to wear distinctive dress
note: A requirement that Jews in North Africa, including Jews who had outwardly converted under coercion, wear distinctive clothing.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 191

name: The Ra’avad III dies
note: R. Avraham ben David of Posquières, the Ra'avad III, died on 26 Kislev. He had founded a yeshiva and written major critical glosses.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 191

name: R. Meir Abulafia challenges aspects of Rambam’s philosophy
note: The Ramah of Toledo sent letters to Lunel and northern France expressing concerns about philosophical positions in the Rambam's works and seeking restrictions on their study.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 191

name: R. Yaakov HaChasid records a responsum in Min HaShamayim
note: A dated entry in R. Yaakov HaChasid's responsa collection Min HaShamayim on 29 Elul 1203.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 191

name: R. Baruch ben Yitzchak II composes Sefer HaTeruma
note: A disciple of the Ri, R. Baruch ben Yitzchak II, composed Sefer HaTeruma around this period.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 191

name: R. Avraham ben Natan HaYarchi settles in Spain and writes Sefer HaManhig
note: After travelling through Germany and Provence, R. Avraham ben Natan HaYarchi settled in Spain and composed Sefer HaManhig.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 191

name: The Rambam dies in Fustat
note: Maimonides died on 20 Tevet 1204. His son R. Avraham succeeded him in communal leadership.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 191

name: R. Avraham Maimuni succeeds the Rambam
note: The Rambam's nineteen-year-old son R. Avraham succeeded him after his death.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 191

name: Jews are killed and expelled from Halle
note: A number of Jews were killed in Halle and the survivors expelled.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 191

name: Béziers massacre kills about two hundred Jews
note: A massacre at Béziers on 19 Av in which about two hundred Jews were killed.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 192

name: English Jews are imprisoned for ransom by royal order
note: Jews being imprisoned in England on royal orders in order to extract ransom.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 192

name: Three hundred Torah scholars migrate from France and England to Eretz Yisrael
note: An aliyah of roughly 300 Talmud scholars from France and England to Eretz Yisrael.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 192

name: Pope Innocent III orders Jews to wear a distinguishing badge
note: A papal order requiring Jews to wear a badge marking them off from the surrounding population; implementation varied across Europe for centuries.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 192

name: English Jews pay for exemptions from the badge requirement
note: Many Jews in England paid money to obtain exemptions from the badge requirement.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 192

name: R. Yehuda HaChasid dies in Regensburg
note: R. Yehuda HaChasid, a leading figure of Chassidei Ashkenaz and author associated with Sefer HaChasidim, died in Regensburg.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 192

name: Erfurt Jewish community is massacred
note: Erfurt Jewish community is massacred.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 192

name: Jews of Sicily and Pisa are ordered to wear a blue badge and grow beards
note: Distinctive-dress regulations imposed on Jews in Sicily and Pisa.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 192

name: Jews are expelled from Cremona and Pavia
note: The expulsion of Jews from Cremona and Pavia in northern Italy, while noting later resettlement.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 192

name: R. Ezra of Girona dies
note: R. Ezra of Girona, an early kabbalist and teacher of the Ramban, died on 9 Tevet.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 192

name: R. Shmuel HaSardi composes Sefer HaTerumot
note: R. Shmuel HaSardi, a contemporary and disciple of the Ramban, and his Sefer HaTerumot is placed in this period.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 192

name: Jews of Wiener Neustadt are attacked for eleven days
note: Anti-Jewish rioters attacked the Jews of Wiener Neustadt for eleven days.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 192

name: Jews in Astorga are killed and forcibly converted
note: Killings and forced conversion of Jews in Astorga.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 192

name: Jews are massacred in Marrakesh
note: A massacre of Jews in Marrakesh in 1232.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 192

name: The Maimonidean controversy intensifies in Provence
note: R. Shlomo ben Avraham of Montpellier sought restrictions on philosophical study, including works of the Rambam. The dispute drew in leading scholars including the Ramban and Radak.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 193

name: Seven Jews are tortured and burned at Bischofsheim
note: Seven Jews being tortured and burned at the stake at Bischofsheim on 10 Shevat.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 193

name: Fulda blood libel leads to the killing of thirty-four Jews
note: The deaths of thirty-four Jews at Fulda in a blood-libel episode.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 193

name: R. Moshe of Coucy campaigns for mitzvah observance across Provence and Spain
note: R. Moshe of Coucy travelled through Provence and Spain encouraging religious observance, including tefillin, and opposing intermarriage.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 193

name: R. Moshe of Coucy composes Sefer Mitzvot Gadol
note: The composition of the Sefer Mitzvot Gadol (SemaG), a major halachic work drawing on the Rambam, is placed in this period.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 193

name: Rampaging mobs kill more than 2,500 Jews in France
note: Widespread attacks in France in which more than 2,500 Jews were killed.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 193

name: Narbonne is spared and institutes a local Purim
note: Narbonne is spared and institutes a local Purim.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 193

name: R. Avraham Maimuni dies
note: R. Avraham Maimuni, son and successor of the Rambam, died on 18 Kislev 1237.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 193

name: R. David HaNagid succeeds R. Avraham Maimuni
note: R. David HaNagid succeeded his father R. Avraham Maimuni in the Maimonidean leadership line.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 193

name: R. Elazar Roke’ach composes Sefer Roke’ach
note: The halachic, customs and ethical work Sefer Roke'ach is placed in this period.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 193

name: Pope Gregory IX orders confiscation of the Talmud and other Jewish books
note: A papal order in 1239 directing the confiscation of copies of the Talmud and other Jewish books.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 193

name: Copies of the Talmud are confiscated across France
note: Following the papal directive, copies of the Talmud were seized in France in Adar II 1240.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 193

name: The Paris Disputation puts the Talmud on trial
note: R. Yechiel of Paris and other Jewish scholars were compelled to defend the Talmud against accusations associated with the convert Nicholas Donin.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 193

name: Jews are expelled from Brittany
note: The expulsion of all Jews from the duchy of Brittany in Tammuz 1240.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 193

name: Frankfurt Jewish quarter is destroyed and most Jews are massacred
note: The destruction of Frankfurt's Jewish quarter and the killing of most of its Jews on 14 Sivan.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 193

name: Jews in Bohemia are killed during the Tatar invasion
note: The deaths of many Jews in Bohemia amid the Tatar invasion.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 193

name: King James I orders Jews in Christian Spain to attend conversion sermons
note: A royal order in the Crown of Aragon requiring Jews to attend Christian conversion sermons.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 193

name: Twenty-four wagonloads of Talmud manuscripts are burned in Paris
note: A huge collection of handwritten Talmudic and other Jewish books was publicly burned in Paris after the 1240 disputation, a major blow to French Torah scholarship.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 193

name: Belitz host-desecration accusation leads to Jews being burned
note: This is identified as the first recorded ritual-desecration or 'host desecration' accusation, resulting in Jews being burned to death.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 194

name: Kitzingen blood libel kills eleven Jews
note: The killing of eleven Jews at Kitzingen after a blood-libel accusation.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 194

name: Khwarazmian and Egyptian forces sack Jerusalem
note: Khwarazmian and Egyptian forces sack Jerusalem.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 194

name: Pope Innocent IV orders further burnings of the Talmud
note: An additional papal order for Talmud burnings on 26 Adar.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 194

name: R. Meir HaLevi Abulafia (the Ramah) dies in Toledo
note: The Ramah of Toledo, author of Yad Ramah and a participant in the Maimonidean controversy, died on 18 Nissan.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 194

name: Jews of Meknes are killed and forcibly converted under a radical regime
note: Killings and forced conversions to Islam in Meknes following the rise of a new radical government.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 194

name: Emperor Frederick II rejects the Fulda blood-libel charge
note: After investigation, Emperor Frederick II concluded that the Fulda blood-libel accusation was false.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 194

name: Pope Innocent IV states that blood-libel accusations are false
note: Innocent IV stating in 1247 that blood-libel accusations against Jews were false.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 194

name: Valréas blood libel brings torture, killings and confiscations
note: Jews in Valréas were tortured; some were mutilated or killed and the remaining Jews were imprisoned, with property confiscated.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 194

name: Christians in France are forbidden contact with Jews
note: A French restriction forbidding Christians from having contact with Jews.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 194

name: Jews of Tunisia are required to wear a distinctive badge
note: Muslim rulers required the Jews of Tunisia to wear a special badge.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 194

name: A new Egyptian regime brings worsening conditions for Jews
note: A new government beginning in Egypt around 1250 oppressed Jews and that conditions deteriorated across the surrounding North African region.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 194

name: Pope Innocent IV authorizes torture in inquisitorial proceedings
note: The authorization of torture in inquisitorial investigations, a development that later exposed Jews to coercive heresy proceedings.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 194

name: Pope Innocent IV orders the expulsion of Jews from Vienne
note: A papal order in Av for all Jews to be expelled from Vienne in France.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 194

name: A Jewish participant in the Cluny religious debate is killed
note: A Jewish participant in a religious disputation at Cluny was killed by a Christian knight.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 195

name: Lincoln blood libel leads to killings of prominent Jews
note: The killing of prominent English Jews in the Lincoln blood-libel affair in Elul 1255.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 195

name: Chief Rabbi R. Eliyahu Menachem is removed for refusing to enforce a heavy tax
note: The removal of R. Eliyahu Menachem ben Moshe from his position as Chief Rabbi in London after he refused to force Jews to pay a heavy tax.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 195

name: Jews of Rome are required to wear a Jewish badge
note: A requirement that all Jews in Rome wear a distinctive badge.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 195

name: Jews of Mainz are required to wear a Jewish badge
note: A distinctive-badge requirement for the Jews of Mainz.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 195

name: R. Yechiel of Paris leaves France for Eretz Yisrael
note: R. Yechiel of Paris left France to settle in Eretz Yisrael at a time of Mongol military pressure in the region.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 195

name: R. Tzidkiyah ben Avraham composes Shibbolei HaLeket
note: The Italian halachic and customs work Shibbolei HaLeket is placed in this period.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 195

name: The Ramban is compelled to take part in the Disputation of Barcelona
note: King James I compelled the Ramban to debate the convert Pablo Christiani in Barcelona in 1263.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 195

name: Royal censorship targets Christian references in the Talmud
note: Royal censorship targets Christian references in the Talmud.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 195

name: The Ramban leaves Aragon after the Barcelona controversy
note: The controversy following the disputation ultimately forced the Ramban to leave Aragon.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 195

name: Rabbenu Yonah of Girona dies
note: Rabbenu Yonah Gerondi, author of Sha'arei Teshuva and a major participant in the Maimonidean controversy, died in 1263.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 195

name: Jews of Arnstadt are massacred by rioters
note: An anti-Jewish massacre at Arnstadt on 11 Av.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 195

name: Twenty Jews are killed in Koblenz
note: The killing of twenty Jews in Koblenz.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 195

name: R. Avraham, a convert to Judaism from Augsburg, is killed
note: R. Avraham, a ger tzedek from Augsburg, was killed on 22 Kislev.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 195

name: Twelve Jews are killed in Cologne
note: The killing of twelve Jews in Cologne in Tammuz.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 195

name: Polish Jews are ordered to wear distinctive hats
note: Orders in parts of Poland requiring Jews to wear special hats.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 195

name: Jews in Poland, Austria and Silesia are required to wear distinctive hats
note: A wider order required Jews in Poland, Austria and Silesia to wear distinctive hats.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 195

name: The Ramban settles in Eretz Yisrael
note: After leaving Iberia, the Ramban arrived in Eretz Yisrael and visited Jerusalem.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 195

name: The Ramban renews organized Jewish communal life in Jerusalem
note: Finding Jerusalem nearly without a functioning Jewish community, the Ramban helped organize a minyan and established a house of prayer, helping renew Jewish settlement in the city.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 195

name: Spanish Jews are exempted from the badge but required to wear a round cape
note: Jews in Spain were exempted from the badge requirement but required to wear a distinctive round cape instead.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 196

name: French Jews are ordered to wear a yellow badge
note: A royal order requiring all Jews of France to wear a yellow badge.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 196

name: Jews are expelled from Carpentras
note: The expulsion of Jews from Carpentras, while noting that they returned a few years later after the area's political status changed.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 196

name: The Ramban dies
note: The Ramban's death on 11 Nissan 1270.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 196

name: Proposed expulsion of Brabant’s Jews is replaced by taxation and badge restrictions
note: Proposed expulsion of Brabant’s Jews is replaced by taxation and badge restrictions.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 196

name: Jews are expelled from Worcester
note: The expulsion of all Jews from Worcester.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 196

name: Anti-Jewish riot destroys Jewish homes in Pamplona
note: An anti-Jewish riot in Pamplona in which Jewish houses were destroyed.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 196

name: R. Yitzchak Males of Toulouse is burned by the Inquisition
note: The execution by burning of R. Yitzchak Males, rabbi of Toulouse, on 9 Shevat.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 196

name: Pope Nicholas III orders Jews to attend Christian conversion sermons
note: A papal order requiring Jews to attend conversion sermons, later enforced in England and elsewhere.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 196

name: English Jews are imprisoned and killed in the coin-clipping prosecutions
note: Increasingly restrictive English policy and records mass arrests and killings connected with accusations of circulating counterfeit money.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 196

name: Polish Jews are required to wear a red badge
note: A red-badge requirement for Jews in Poland.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 196

name: London blood libel results in Jewish deaths
note: A blood-libel episode in London in Nissan 1279 in which Jews were killed.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 196

name: Council of Buda restricts Jews from leasing land and mandates the badge
note: A Church Council at Buda requiring Jews to wear a badge and forbidding them from leasing land.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 196

name: R. Yitzchak of Corbeil, author of Sefer Mitzvot Katan, dies
note: The death around 1280 of R. Yitzchak of Corbeil, author of Sefer Mitzvot Katan (SemaK), while noting an alternative earlier date.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 196

name: R. Avraham Abulafia travels toward the pope with a plan to convert him to Judaism
note: Avraham Abulafia travelling toward Rome/Soriano intending to convert Pope Nicholas III. A stake was reportedly prepared for him, but the pope died before the encounter.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 197

name: Mainz blood libel leads to killings and the burning of the synagogue
note: Jews killed in a blood-libel episode at Mainz and the synagogue burned.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 197

name: New blood libel in Mainz leads to further violence
note: Another blood-libel accusation in Mainz in 1283.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 197

name: Bacharach blood libel leads to a massacre
note: A blood-libel accusation in Bacharach and the killing of many Jews in the ensuing massacre.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 197

name: Munich blood libel results in the killing of 180 Jews
note: The killing of 180 Jews in Munich in a blood-libel episode.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 197

name: R. David HaNagid is removed from office in Cairo and leaves for Eretz Yisrael
note: R. David HaNagid is removed from office in Cairo and leaves for Eretz Yisrael.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 197

name: Sefer HaChinuch is composed anonymously around this period
note: The anonymous composition of Sefer HaChinuch is placed around this period; later tradition associated it with the school of the Rashba.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 197

name: Maharam of Rothenburg is captured and imprisoned at Ensisheim
note: Maharam of Rothenburg is captured and imprisoned at Ensisheim.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 197

name: Forty Jews are killed in the Oberwesel blood libel
note: The killing of forty Jews at Oberwesel on the same day that Maharam of Rothenburg was interned.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 197

name: Bacharach massacre follows the Oberwesel persecutions
note: A further massacre in Bacharach in 1287 following the sequence of blood-libel violence in the region.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 197

name: Thirteen Jews are burned at Troyes after a blood-libel prosecution
note: Thirteen Jews being burned at the stake by the Inquisition at Troyes on 20 Iyar after a blood-libel accusation.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 197

name: Blood libel in Neuchâtel leads to Jewish deaths
note: Jews being killed at Neuchâtel in a blood-libel episode.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 197

name: Jews are expelled from Anjou
note: The expulsion of Jews from Anjou.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 197

name: Jews are expelled from Le Mans
note: The expulsion of Jews from Le Mans.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 197

name: R. Menachem Recanati advances written Kabbalistic literature
note: R. Menachem Recanati's kabbalistic biblical commentary and Piskei HaRecanti is placed in the intellectual developments around 1290.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 197

name: R. Moshe de León circulates the work known as the Zohar
note: R. Moshe de León circulates the work known as the Zohar.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 197

name: The Tosafist era draws to a close
note: About 1290 as the end of the main Tosafist era after nearly two centuries of French and German Tosafist scholarship.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 198

name: R. Peretz of Corbeil composes Tosafot Rabbenu Peretz
note: R. Peretz ben Yitzchak of Corbeil composed one of the late Tosafist collections, portions of which entered the standard printed Tosafot.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 198

name: R. Eliezer of Touques composes and edits Tosafot Tuch
note: R. Eliezer of Touques produced Tosafot Tuch, an abbreviated and edited Tosafist collection that became a major component of the standard printed Tosafot.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 198

name: R. David HaNagid is reinstated in Cairo
note: R. David HaNagid returning to his Cairo position five years after his removal.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 198

name: All Jews are expelled from England
note: All Jews are expelled from England.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 198

name: Jews in Naples, Bari and other southern Italian towns are massacred and forcibly baptized
note: Blood-libel violence in southern Italy involving massacres, forced baptisms and migration from communities including Naples and Bari.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 198

name: Maharam of Rothenburg dies in imprisonment at Ensisheim
note: Maharam of Rothenburg dies in imprisonment at Ensisheim.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 198

name: R. Aharon HaLevi composes Bedek HaBayit and chidushim
note: The Ra'ah's critical and Talmudic writings is placed in this period, including Bedek HaBayit, his critique of the Rashba's Torat HaBayit.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 199

name: The Rashba writes Mishmeret HaBayit in response to the Ra’ah
note: The Rashba responded to the Ra'ah's Bedek HaBayit with Mishmeret HaBayit, initially anonymously.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 199

name: Jews in Iraq are forced to convert to Islam
note: Forced conversions of a number of Jews in Iraq around this time.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 199

name: Bern blood libel leads to killings and expulsion
note: A blood-libel accusation in Bern led to the killing of some Jews and the expulsion of the remainder; return was later allowed after heavy payments and cancellation of debts owed to Jews.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 199

name: Rindfleisch massacres begin and spread across Central Europe
note: Rindfleisch massacres begin and spread across Central Europe.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 199

name: Rindfleisch mob begins its anti-Jewish killing campaign at Röttingen
note: Röttingen is identified as the starting point of the Rindfleisch massacres on 7 Iyar.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 199

name: Jews of Wiener Neustadt are massacred in the Rindfleisch wave
note: A massacre at Wiener Neustadt on 12 Tammuz.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 199

name: Jews of Ifhauben are massacred in the Rindfleisch wave
note: A massacre in a place rendered Ifhauben in Austria on 13 Tammuz.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 199

name: About 250 Jews are killed at Rothenburg ob der Tauber
note: Approximately 250 Jewish deaths at Rothenburg ob der Tauber on 14 Tammuz.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 199

name: Jews of Mergentheim are massacred in the Rindfleisch wave
note: The massacre of the Mergentheim Jewish community on 18 Tammuz.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 199

name: Jews of Würzburg are massacred in the Rindfleisch wave
note: A massacre of the Würzburg Jewish community on 13 Av.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 199

name: Jews of Bischofsheim are massacred in the Rindfleisch wave
note: A massacre at Bischofsheim on 14 Av.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 199

name: R. Mordechai ben Hillel and his family are killed at Nuremberg
note: R. Mordechai ben Hillel and his family are killed at Nuremberg.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 199

name: R. Avraham ben Baruch and his family are killed in Mainz
note: R. Avraham ben Baruch, sometimes identified as a brother of Maharam of Rothenburg, was killed with his wife and children in Mainz.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 199

name: Korneuburg ritual-desecration libel kills ten Jews
note: Ten Jews were killed in Korneuburg in a ritual-desecration accusation during the wider period of anti-Jewish violence.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 199

name: R. Meir HaKohen, author of Hagahot Maimoniyot, is killed with his family
note: R. Meir ben Yekutiel HaKohen, author of Hagahot Maimoniyot, was killed with his family during the Rindfleisch massacres.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 199

name: Two hundred Jews are killed in Heilbronn
note: The killing of about 200 Jews in Heilbronn on 12 Cheshvan.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 199

name: Jews of Renchen are massacred in a continuation of the Rindfleisch violence
note: A massacre of the Jewish community of Renchen in 1301 as a continuation of the earlier Rindfleisch persecutions.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 199

name: Barcelona Jews are ordered to kneel when passing Christian priests
note: A degrading regulation requiring Jews in Barcelona to kneel when passing Christian priests.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 199

name: Jews of Gotha are attacked in the continuing persecution wave
note: An attack on the Jews of Gotha as part of the continuing post-Rindfleisch violence.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 200

name: Jews of Weißensee are massacred
note: The massacre of the Jewish community of Weißensee on 7 Nissan.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 200

name: Egyptian Jews face forced conversion and mandatory yellow turbans
note: Forced conversions of many Jews in Egypt and a requirement that Jews wear yellow turbans.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 200

name: The Rosh leaves Germany with his family
note: Concerned that he might be imprisoned for ransom like his teacher Maharam of Rothenburg, R. Asher ben Yechiel (the Rosh) left Germany with his family.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 200

name: R. Yitzchak of Düren composes Sha’arei Dura
note: The composition of Sha'arei Dura, an influential Ashkenazi work on dietary law, is placed in this period.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 200

name: The Rashba restricts philosophical study for younger students
note: After an appeal by R. Abba Mari of Montpellier, the Rashba issued a limited ban on philosophical study below age twenty-five while continuing to affirm the greatness of the Rambam and allowing medicine.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 200

name: The Rosh arrives in Barcelona and then becomes rabbi of Toledo
note: The Rosh arrived in Barcelona in 1305, was received by the Rashba, and soon became rabbi of Toledo, bringing the Franco-German Tosafist style of Talmud study into Spain.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 200

name: All Jews are expelled from France
note: All Jews are expelled from France.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 200

name: Rabbenu Yerucham leaves France as a refugee
note: Rabbenu Yerucham was among the scholars driven from France by the 1306 expulsion.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 200

name: R. Aharon, father of R. Menachem ibn Zerach, leaves France
note: R. Aharon, father of Menachem ibn Zerach, among the refugees of the 1306 expulsion.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 200

name: R. Shimshon of Chinon leaves France
note: R. Shimshon ben Yitzchak of Chinon, author of Sefer Keritut, was among the refugees leaving France.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 200

name: R. Aharon HaKohen of Lunel leaves France
note: R. Aharon ben Yaakov HaKohen of Lunel, author of Orchot Chayim, was among the expelled scholars.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 200

name: Eshtori HaParchi begins refugee journey from France toward Spain, Egypt and Eretz Yisrael
note: Eshtori HaParchi was driven from France and travelled through Spain and Egypt before settling in Eretz Yisrael, where he later wrote Kaftor VaFerach.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 200

name: Maharam of Rothenburg’s body is released for burial
note: After fourteen years, the body of Maharam of Rothenburg was released for burial through the efforts of R. Alexander Susskind Wimpfen, who was later buried near him.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 200

name: A mob kills 110 Jews at Born in Limburg
note: The killing of 110 Jews by a mob at Born in Limburg.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 200

name: Jews are killed at Louvain after refusing forced baptism
note: Many Jews being killed in neighboring Louvain after refusing forced baptism.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 200

name: The Rashba dies in Barcelona
note: R. Shlomo ibn Aderet (the Rashba), one of the leading halachic authorities of medieval Spain, died in Barcelona.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 200

name: The Rosh becomes the leading halachic authority after the Rashba’s death
note: The Rosh as becoming the leading halachic authority after the Rashba's death, with students coming to Toledo from distant European communities.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 201

name: Southern Italian forced converts are punished for returning secretly to Judaism
note: Severe punishment of southern Italian forced converts who had resumed Jewish practice in secret.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 201

name: Jews are killed in ritual-desecration and blood-libel accusations in Fürstenfeld and Judenburg
note: Jewish deaths in accusations at Fürstenfeld and Judenburg in Styria.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 201

name: Jews are permitted to return to France
note: Louis X allowed Jews to return to France nine years after the 1306 expulsion.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 201

name: The Ritva composes a major Talmud commentary
note: The Ritva's extensive Talmud commentary and other writings is placed in Spain around this period.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 201

name: The Inquisition orders Talmud burnings in Toulouse and Perpignan
note: The burning of the Talmud under inquisitorial order in Toulouse and Perpignan.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 201

name: Several Jews are burned at the stake in Tudela
note: Several Jews being burned at the stake in Tudela in the same year as the French Talmud burnings.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 201

name: Pastoureaux Crusade attacks Jewish communities across France
note: The Shepherds' Crusade moved through France toward Spain, attacking Jews in many towns, looting, killing and forcing conversions.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 201

name: About 500 Jewish refugees are killed at Verdun
note: About 500 Jewish refugees are killed at Verdun.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 201

name: All Jews are expelled from Milan
note: The expulsion of all Jews from Milan.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 201

name: Jews of Rome are expelled before withdrawal of the order can reach the city
note: An expulsion order issued from Avignon was later withdrawn, but the Jews of Rome had already been expelled before news of the withdrawal arrived.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 201

name: Well-poisoning accusation leads to mass burnings in Chinon, Tours and Vitry
note: 160 Jews burned on Rosh Hashanah in Chinon, Tours and Vitry after accusations of poisoning wells in league with local lepers.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 201

name: R. Eliezer ben Yosef and his brothers are killed in the French well-poisoning persecutions
note: R. Eliezer ben Yosef, a relative of R. Peretz of Corbeil, and his two brothers were among those killed in the 1321 persecutions.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 201

name: Jews are expelled from additional parts of France
note: Further expulsions of Jews from parts of France in 1322.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 201

name: The Talmud is burned in Rome
note: A Talmud burning in Rome.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 201

name: Constance ritual-desecration libel kills twenty-seven Jews
note: The killing of twenty-seven Jews in Constance in a ritual-desecration libel.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 201

name: The Rosh dies in Toledo
note: R. Asher ben Yechiel (the Rosh) died in Cheshvan 1327 after establishing a major halachic school in Toledo.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 201

name: R. Yehuda, son of the Rosh, succeeds him
note: R. Yehuda, one of the Rosh's younger sons, succeeded his father.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 202

name: Anti-Jewish riots kill thousands in Navarre
note: Roughly 6,000 Jewish deaths in anti-Jewish riots in the province of Navarre.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 202

name: Menachem ibn Zerach survives the Estella massacre and relocates to Toledo
note: Menachem ibn Zerach survived the massacre in Estella after his parents and four brothers were killed, then went to Toledo to study.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 202

name: The Tur urges Jews to leave dangerous conditions in Germany
note: R. Yaakov ben Asher (the Tur) encouraging Jews to leave Germany because of continuing danger.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 202

name: Überlingen blood libel kills about 300 Jews and the synagogue is burned
note: Roughly 300 Jews killed after a blood-libel accusation at Überlingen, with the synagogue set on fire.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 202

name: Rabbenu Yerucham composes Meisharim and Adam VeChava
note: Rabbenu Yerucham's halachic works Meisharim and Adam VeChava is placed around this time.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 202

name: Polish Jews receive renewed guarantees of rights
note: Renewed promises of certain rights to the Jews of Poland in Cheshvan 1334.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 202

name: Armleder bands devastate Jewish communities in Germany and Alsace
note: Peasant bands known as the Armleder roamed Germany and Alsace for years, killing Jews and ravaging roughly 120 communities.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 202

name: About 1,500 Jews are killed at Ribeauvillé
note: Approximately 1,500 Jewish deaths at Ribeauvillé during the Armleder violence.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 202

name: Deggendorf ritual-desecration libel destroys the Jewish community
note: The killing of all Jews in Deggendorf after a ritual-desecration accusation.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 202

name: R. Shem Tov ibn Gaon composes Migdal Oz
note: R. Shem Tov ibn Gaon, a disciple of the Rashba who emigrated to Eretz Yisrael, composed Migdal Oz, a commentary on the Rambam's Mishneh Torah.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 202

name: Massacres kill many Jews in Bohemia
note: Widespread Jewish deaths in massacres in Bohemia.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 202

name: The Ralbag completes major biblical and philosophical works
note: Ralbag's biblical commentary and Milchamot HaShem is placed around this time.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 202

name: The Ralbag develops mathematical and astronomical work including the Jacob staff
note: Ralbag's mathematical work and credits him with an astronomical measuring instrument known as the Jacob staff.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 202

name: Pulkau ritual-desecration persecution spreads across twenty-seven towns
note: Pulkau ritual-desecration persecution spreads across twenty-seven towns.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 202

name: R. Yaakov ben Asher composes the Arba’ah Turim
note: The Tur's encyclopedic halachic code, whose four-part arrangement later shaped the Shulchan Aruch, is dated to around 1340.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 202

name: R. Yaakov ben Asher dies in Toledo
note: The Tur's death is placed in Toledo in 1340, while noting an alternative tradition of 1348.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 202

name: R. David Abudraham composes his prayer guide
note: R. David Abudraham's influential prayer guide and commentary is placed around 1342.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 202

name: R. Shimon, son of the Rosh, dies in a plague
note: R. Shimon, the eighth son of the Rosh, died in a plague on 12 Elul.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 202

name: The Ralbag dies
note: R. Levi ben Gershom (Gersonides/Ralbag) died on 6 Iyar 1344.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 203

name: R. Vidal of Tolosa composes Maggid Mishneh
note: R. Vidal of Tolosa's Maggid Mishneh commentary on the Rambam is placed in this period.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 203

name: The Ran composes commentaries on the Rif and Talmud
note: The Ran is identified as a contemporary of R. Vidal and notes his commentaries on the Rif and sections of the Talmud.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 203

name: Black Death plague reaches Jewish communities across Europe
note: The plague spreading across Central and Western Europe and causing enormous mortality among Jews and non-Jews alike.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 203

name: Tortured well-poisoning confession at Lausanne fuels anti-Jewish massacres
note: A forced confession under torture at Lausanne alleging that Jews poisoned wells; the accusation then spread rapidly through Europe.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 203

name: More than three quarters of Zaragoza’s Jews die in the Black Death
note: Exceptionally high plague mortality among the Jews of Zaragoza.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 203

name: Vienna’s Jewish cemetery is enlarged because of Black Death mortality
note: Vienna did not experience a massacre in this phase but Jewish plague deaths were so numerous that the cemetery had to be expanded.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 203

name: Jews of Bern are burned after the well-poisoning accusation spreads
note: Jews in Bern being burned after the Lausanne accusations spread.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 203

name: Jews of Colmar are imprisoned and later burned
note: The Jews of Colmar were imprisoned on a well-poisoning accusation and later burned.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 203

name: Hundreds of Basel Jews are burned and children forcibly baptized
note: About 600 Jews burned at Basel and about 140 children subjected to forced baptism. Modern victim estimates vary.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 203

name: Speyer Jews perish amid Black Death persecution
note: Jews at Speyer setting their houses on fire rather than face destruction by a mob.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 203

name: Jews of Freiburg are killed in Black Death persecution
note: The killing of Freiburg's Jews during the Black Death persecutions.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 203

name: Jews of Überlingen are massacred during the Black Death persecutions
note: The massacre of Überlingen's Jews on 22 Adar I.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 203

name: Strasbourg massacre burns roughly two thousand Jews
note: Roughly 2,000 Jews burned to death at Strasbourg during the Black Death persecutions.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 203

name: Jews are expelled from Burgdorf
note: The expulsion of all Jews from Burgdorf during the Black Death persecution wave.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 203

name: Zurich Jews are burned and expelled
note: Burnings of Jews in Zurich followed by expulsion of the survivors.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 203

name: Worms Jewish community perishes in flames
note: The Jews of Worms setting their homes on fire and perishing during the Black Death persecution.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 203

name: Jews of Mühlhausen are killed during the Black Death persecutions
note: The killing of the Jews of Mühlhausen around Passover.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 203

name: Erfurt massacre destroys the Jewish community
note: A figure of about 3,000 Jews killed at Erfurt. Modern scholarship gives a wide range of estimates.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 203

name: Breslau anti-Jewish riot after a disastrous fire kills sixty Jews
note: Sixty Jewish deaths in Breslau amid riots following a major fire.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 203

name: R. Yehuda, son of the Rosh, dies in the Black Death
note: R. Yehuda, son and successor of the Rosh, died of plague together with some members of his family.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 203

name: Frankfurt Jewish community is massacred
note: A massacre of Frankfurt's Jews on the eve of Tisha B'Av during the Black Death persecutions.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 203

name: About 300 Jews are killed at Tàrrega
note: The killing of about 300 Jews at Tàrrega in Catalonia.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 203

name: Mainz Jewish community is destroyed in mass death and fire
note: Jewish resistance against a mob at Mainz followed by approximately 6,000 Jews dying in burning houses.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 203

name: Cologne Jewish community perishes during the Black Death persecutions
note: The Jews of Cologne dying in a similar mass-burning episode shortly after Mainz.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 203

name: Krems Jewish community is massacred
note: A Black Death riot massacre at Krems.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 203

name: Jews of Augsburg are attacked in Black Death persecution
note: The killing of Augsburg's Jews in the continuing Black Death violence.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 203

name: Hundreds of Nuremberg Jews are killed and burned
note: About 560 Jewish deaths at Nuremberg.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 204

name: Jews are massacred in Hanover during the Black Death persecutions
note: A massacre of Hanover's Jewish community.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 204

name: Jews are massacred in Brussels during the Black Death persecutions
note: A massacre of Jews in Brussels in the continuing wave of violence.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 204

name: R. Peretz HaKohen flees Provence and settles in Barcelona
note: R. Peretz HaKohen left Provence because of the Black Death massacres and settled in Barcelona, where he became a rabbi alongside the Ran.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 204

name: All Jews of Cheb are massacred
note: The complete massacre of Cheb's Jewish community.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 204

name: Black Death persecutions leave more than 300 Jewish communities destroyed
note: The Black Death massacres and expulsions as destroying more than 300 Jewish communities, especially in Germany.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 204

name: Jewish migration accelerates eastward toward Poland-Lithuania
note: Jewish migration accelerates eastward toward Poland-Lithuania.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 204

name: A Christian-Muslim mob kills about 1,200 Jews in Toledo
note: About 1,200 Jews killed in an attack on Toledo's Jewish quarter.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 204

name: Hundreds of Jews are killed in Catalonia
note: Hundreds of Jewish deaths in Catalonia on the day after Tisha B'Av.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 204

name: Breslau Jews are killed in riots and survivors expelled
note: Anti-Jewish riots in Breslau following a fire killed many Jews; the remaining Jews were expelled.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 204

name: All Jews are expelled from Hungary and soon permitted to return
note: A complete expulsion of Hungary's Jews followed by readmission after a short period.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 204

name: Shmuel HaLevi Abulafia is arrested, tortured to death and his wealth confiscated
note: The fall of the wealthy Castilian Jewish courtier Shmuel ben Meir HaLevi Abulafia.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 204

name: R. Mattityahu Treves is appointed Chief Rabbi of France
note: The king of France appointed R. Mattityahu ben Yosef Treves Chief Rabbi after he returned to Paris and opened a yeshiva.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 204

name: Barcelona ritual-desecration accusation kills three Jews and imprisons the community
note: Three Jews were killed and the Jewish community was held prisoner in the synagogue for three days after a ritual-desecration accusation.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 204

name: The Ran, Rivash and members of the Crescas family are imprisoned
note: The imprisonment of the Ran, R. Chisdai Crescas and his grandson, the young Rivash, and others, possibly in connection with the same accusation.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 204

name: Castilian civil war brings major Jewish casualties
note: Many Jewish deaths during civil war in Castile and reports that about 8,000 Jews had been killed in Toledo.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 204

name: Brussels ritual-desecration accusation leads to mass burning and expulsion
note: Hundreds of Jews were burned alive in Brussels in a ritual-desecration accusation; the remaining Jews were expelled.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 204

name: Jews are tortured and burned at Huesca in a ritual-desecration libel
note: Torture and burning of Jews in Huesca.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 204

name: Anti-Jewish rioters kill Jews in Paris
note: Jewish deaths in anti-Jewish riots in Paris in Kislev.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 204

name: R. Yisrael of Krems composes Hagahot Ashri
note: R. Yisrael of Krems's Hagahot Ashri on the Rosh's Talmud commentary is placed in this period.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 204

name: Maharam HaLevi introduces rabbinic semicha as a qualification system
note: R. Meir ben Baruch HaLevi of Vienna introduced a formal semicha system intended to ensure minimum qualifications for rabbis handling marriage, divorce and related law.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 204

name: R. Yeshayahu ben Abba Mari is empowered as Chief Rabbi in France
note: Maharam HaLevi empowered R. Yeshayahu ben Abba Mari to act as Chief Rabbi in France and confer semicha, producing a dispute with R. Yochanan Treves.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 204

name: Prague massacre kills about 3,000 Jews
note: Approximately 3,000 Jews killed in Prague the day after Passover, with houses burned and the cemetery desecrated.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 205

name: R. Yitzchak Abohab I composes Menorat HaMa’or
note: The composition of the ethical work Menorat HaMa'or is placed around this time.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 205

name: Mass anti-Jewish violence and forced conversion sweep the Spanish kingdoms
note: A wave of massacres spreading from Seville through Spain and Portugal, accompanied by mass forced conversion and destruction or conversion of synagogues.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 205

name: Seville massacre kills thousands of Jews
note: A figure of about 4,000 Jewish deaths in Seville on 1 Tammuz.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 205

name: Jews are massacred at Jaén in the 1391 violence
note: Jaén among major massacre sites in Tammuz 1391.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 205

name: Jews are massacred at Toledo in the 1391 violence
note: Large-scale Jewish deaths in Toledo during the 1391 wave.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 205

name: Valencia Jewish community is destroyed
note: The destruction of the Valencia Jewish community on 7 Av.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 205

name: Barcelona Jews are massacred in the 1391 violence
note: A massacre in Barcelona as the violence spread through Catalonia.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 205

name: Massacres spread across Catalonia
note: Anti-Jewish violence throughout Catalonia.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 205

name: Palma de Mallorca Jews are massacred
note: A massacre in Palma on 1 Elul.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 205

name: Girona Jews are attacked in the 1391 violence
