note: The Hungarian Jewish parachutist from Eretz Yisrael, who returned to occupied Europe to aid resistance and rescue efforts, was executed after capture.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 293

name: First Kasztner transport of 318 Jews is released to safety
note: A first group of 318 Jews released from Nazi control through negotiations associated with Rudolf Kasztner.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 293

name: Kasztner train group of 1,368 Jews is released from Bergen-Belsen
note: A second, larger group released from Bergen-Belsen and enabled to leave Nazi-controlled Europe.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 293

name: Satmar Rebbe survives through the Kasztner train rescue
note: R. Yoel Teitelbaum of Satmar was among those released from Bergen-Belsen; after the war he spent time in Eretz Yisrael and later settled in New York.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 293

name: Raoul Wallenberg disappears after Soviet forces take him into custody
note: The Swedish diplomat who had helped protect tens of thousands of Hungarian Jews disappeared after being detained by advancing Soviet forces.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 293

name: Soviet troops liberate Auschwitz
note: Soviet troops entered the Auschwitz complex and liberated prisoners who had been left behind after mass evacuations.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 293

name: Maria Skobtsova ('Mother Maria of Paris') is killed in Ravensbrück
note: The Russian Orthodox nun who had helped rescue Jews in France was killed by the Nazis shortly before the end of the war.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 293

name: US forces liberate Buchenwald
note: American forces entered Buchenwald as prisoners took control of the camp.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 293

name: US forces reach Mittelbau-Dora and Nordhausen
note: American troops found thousands of corpses and hundreds of sick prisoners at the Mittelbau-Dora/Nordhausen complex.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 294

name: Lili Jacob discovers the Auschwitz Album at Dora
note: Holocaust survivor Lili Jacob found an SS photograph album documenting the arrival and selection of Hungarian Jews at Auschwitz-Birkenau, recognizing relatives and people from her home community.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 294

name: British forces liberate Bergen-Belsen
note: British troops liberated Bergen-Belsen and encountered tens of thousands of desperately ill survivors.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 293

name: US forces liberate Dachau
note: American forces liberated Dachau near the end of April 1945.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 293

name: US forces liberate Mauthausen
note: American forces liberated Mauthausen during the final days of the war in Europe.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 293

name: Nazi Germany surrenders and World War II ends in Europe
note: Germany's unconditional surrender ended the European war and Nazi rule.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 294

name: Hitler dies as Nazi Germany collapses
note: Hitler's reported suicide shortly before Germany's surrender.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 294

name: Theresienstadt is liberated
note: The ghetto-camp that had served as a major transit point for deportations was liberated shortly after Germany's surrender.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 294

name: Atomic bombs are dropped on Hiroshima and Nagasaki
note: The United States used atomic bombs against Hiroshima and Nagasaki, accelerating the end of the Pacific war and opening the nuclear age.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 294

name: Jewish survivors enter displaced-persons camps across Allied-occupied Europe
note: Many Holocaust survivors could not return home or had no homes to return to. Allied authorities housed large numbers in displaced-persons camps while survivors searched for relatives and future destinations.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 294

name: Many liberated camp survivors die from disease and severe starvation damage
note: Liberation did not immediately end mortality: many survivors died because of extreme weakness, disease and the physiological effects of prolonged starvation.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 294

name: Approximately six million Jews have been murdered in the Holocaust
note: By the end of the war, Nazi Germany and its allies and collaborators had murdered approximately six million Jews.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 294

name: Jewish underground frees detainees from the Atlit camp
note: A Jewish underground force attacked the British detention camp at Atlit and freed 208 Jewish detainees held under Britain's restrictive immigration policy.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 295

name: Postwar Jewish immigration campaign challenges British restrictions
note: Jewish underground and immigration organizations continued efforts to bring Holocaust survivors and displaced persons into Mandatory Palestine despite British restrictions and interceptions.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 295

name: U.S. Army publishes the Survivors' Talmud in Germany
note: An edition of the Talmud was produced in Germany for Jewish displaced persons and survivors, becoming a symbol of postwar religious rebuilding.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 295

name: Jewish underground destroys bridges in the Night of the Bridges campaign
note: Jewish resistance forces attacked bridges linking Mandatory Palestine to neighboring territories as conflict with British rule intensified.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 295

name: British authorities arrest Jewish political leaders in the Black Sabbath crackdown
note: British forces arrested Jewish Agency and other Yishuv leaders during a large-scale crackdown on underground activity.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 295

name: Kielce pogrom kills forty-two Jewish Holocaust survivors
note: A postwar antisemitic pogrom in Kielce killed more than forty Jews and accelerated Jewish flight from Poland.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 295

name: King David Hotel bombing destroys British headquarters in Jerusalem
note: King David Hotel bombing destroys British headquarters in Jerusalem.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 295

name: Nuremberg executions follow convictions of senior Nazi leaders
note: Ten senior Nazi officials sentenced to death by the International Military Tribunal were executed after convictions for war crimes and crimes against humanity.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 295

name: Vatican instruction opposes return of some baptized Jewish children to their families
note: Vatican instruction opposes return of some baptized Jewish children to their families.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 295

name: Angelo Roncalli assists efforts to return Jewish children despite Vatican instructions
note: Angelo Roncalli, later Pope John XXIII, did not follow restrictive instructions and assisted Jewish families seeking children hidden during the war.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 295

name: First volume of Encyclopaedia Talmudit is published
note: The first volume of the Talmud Encyclopedia was published in Eretz Yisrael under the editorship of R. Shlomo Yosef Zevin.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 295

name: First volume of Otzar HaPoskim is published
note: A major encyclopedic halachic project on Even HaEzer began publication under editors including R. Yitzchak Herzog, R. Isser Zalman Meltzer and R. Shlomo Yosef Zevin.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 295

name: British authorities send intercepted Jewish immigrants to Cyprus
note: Passengers from immigrant ships reaching Mandatory Palestine without British authorization were transferred to detention camps in Cyprus.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 295

name: British seize the Exodus 1947 and return its passengers to Europe
note: British forces intercepted the Exodus carrying more than 4,500 Jewish displaced persons; after a violent boarding, the passengers were ultimately returned to the British zone in Germany.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 295

name: United Nations adopts the Palestine partition plan
note: UN General Assembly Resolution 181 recommended termination of the British Mandate and partition into Arab and Jewish states, with Jerusalem under a special international regime.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 296

name: Civil war begins in Mandatory Palestine after the UN partition vote
note: Fighting between Palestinian Arab and Jewish forces escalated immediately after the partition resolution, with support and volunteers arriving from surrounding Arab countries.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 296

name: Aden riots kill seventy-five Jews
note: Anti-Jewish riots in Aden following the partition vote killed dozens of Jews and devastated Jewish property.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 296

name: Aleppo riots destroy synagogues and accelerate Jewish flight from Syria
note: Anti-Jewish violence in Aleppo destroyed synagogues and accelerated the departure of the city's Jews.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 296

name: British authorities turn away another ship carrying Holocaust survivors
note: A crowded immigrant ship reaching Eretz Yisrael and being denied entry by British authorities.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 296

name: Bombing in central Jerusalem kills Jewish civilians
note: A deadly bombing in central Jerusalem during the escalating pre-state war.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 296

name: Arab forces impose a siege on Jewish Jerusalem
note: Road access to Jerusalem was cut, creating severe shortages for the city's Jewish population.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 296

name: Jewish forces temporarily break the siege of Jerusalem
note: A major supply effort reopened access to Jerusalem during the pre-state fighting.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 296

name: British Mandate over Palestine ends
note: British governmental authority ended and almost all British troops departed as the Mandate terminated.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 296

name: State of Israel is declared in Tel Aviv
note: David Ben-Gurion read the Declaration of the Establishment of the State of Israel on behalf of the People's Council as the British Mandate ended.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 296

name: New Israeli government opens immigration to Jews
note: The provisional government removed British-era restrictions on Jewish immigration; this principle was later formalized in the Law of Return.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 296

name: Arab state armies invade the newly declared State of Israel
note: Following Israel's declaration of independence, armies from Egypt, Transjordan, Syria, Lebanon and Iraq entered the former Mandate territory; Saudi forces also participated under Egyptian command.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 296

name: Egyptian aircraft bomb Tel Aviv at the opening of the interstate war
note: Air attacks on Tel Aviv accompanied the entry of Arab state armies into the war.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 296

name: Jewish Quarter of Jerusalem's Old City falls to the Arab Legion
note: The Jewish Quarter surrendered after intense fighting, and Jewish residents were evacuated from the Old City.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 296

name: Hurva Synagogue is destroyed after the fall of the Jewish Quarter
note: The historic Hurva Synagogue was destroyed after Jordanian Arab Legion forces captured the Jewish Quarter.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 296

name: Burma Road supply route helps relieve the Jerusalem siege
note: A rough bypass road was built to move supplies toward Jerusalem when the main road remained blocked.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 297

name: Mickey Marcus is killed near his headquarters
note: American volunteer officer David 'Mickey' Marcus, serving in the Israeli forces, was accidentally killed by friendly fire.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 297

name: Altalena affair ends in armed confrontation among Jewish forces
note: The Altalena, carrying arms and immigrant fighters for the Irgun, was shelled during a confrontation with the new Israeli government and military; about twenty Jews were killed.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 297

name: Imrei Emes of Ger dies during the siege of Jerusalem
note: R. Avraham Mordechai Alter, the Imrei Emes of Ger, died on Shavuot and was buried in Jerusalem.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 297

name: R. Yisrael Alter becomes the Beis Yisroel of Ger
note: R. Yisrael Alter succeeded his father as the principal Gerer rebbe.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 297

name: Bombing and riots kill Jews in Cairo
note: Twenty Jews killed by a bomb in Cairo's Jewish quarter and more than one hundred killed in sporadic anti-Jewish riots.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 297

name: Last British armed forces leave the country
note: The final British military presence departed after the formal end of the Mandate.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 297

name: Jerusalem is bombed from the air during the war
note: An air raid on Jerusalem during the continuing war.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 297

name: Israeli aircraft bomb Cairo in retaliation
note: Newly acquired Israeli aircraft carried out a retaliatory bombing raid on Cairo.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 297

name: Jerusalem water supply is disrupted during the war
note: Arab forces destroyed a pumping station, worsening the siege conditions in Jerusalem.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 297

name: Palestinian Arab refugee crisis develops during the 1948 war
note: Hundreds of thousands of Palestinian Arabs fled or were expelled from their homes during the 1948 conflict, creating a long-term refugee crisis.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 297

name: First volume of She'arim HaMetzuyanim BeHalacha is published in New York
note: R. Shlomo Zalman Braun published the first volume of his halachic work updating the Kitzur Shulchan Aruch.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 297

name: Jewish Holocaust survivors are attacked in a Plungė blood libel
note: Anti-Jewish violence against survivors in Plungė on the eve of Rosh Hashanah.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 297

name: Britain releases remaining Jewish detainees from Cyprus
note: The remaining roughly 25,000 Jewish detainees were released from Cyprus camps after Israel's independence.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 297

name: Jewish population of Israel reaches about one million
note: Roughly one million Jews living in Israel, nearly 300,000 more than a year earlier.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 297

name: Israel signs armistice agreements with neighboring Arab states
note: Separate armistice agreements with Egypt, Lebanon, Jordan and Syria ended the main phase of the 1948 Arab-Israeli War.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 297

name: War of Independence ends with Jerusalem divided
note: The armistice system left West Jerusalem under Israeli control while the Old City and Western Wall remained under Jordanian control until 1967.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 297

name: Codex records roughly six thousand Jewish military and civilian deaths in the 1948 war
note: About 4,000 Jewish soldiers and 2,000 Jewish civilians killed in the war.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 297

name: R. Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn dies in New York
note: The sixth Lubavitcher Rebbe died after rebuilding a large international network of Torah and communal institutions following his escape from Europe.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 297

name: R. Menachem Mendel Schneerson becomes leader of Chabad-Lubavitch
note: R. Menachem Mendel Schneerson succeeded his father-in-law and greatly expanded Chabad's worldwide institutional network.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 297

name: Mass aliyah from Iraq begins
note: Mass aliyah from Iraq begins.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 298

name: Operation Magic Carpet brings most remaining Yemenite Jews to Israel
note: A large JDC-organized airlift brought tens of thousands of Yemenite Jews through Aden to Israel, effectively ending most of the ancient Yemenite Jewish community.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 298

name: Mass immigration creates conflict over religious and cultural absorption policies
note: Controversy over secularizing pressures placed on some new immigrants from traditional Middle Eastern communities.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 298

name: Allegations emerge concerning missing Yemenite and other immigrant children
note: Families from Yemenite and other immigrant communities reported children disappearing after hospitalization or institutional care; the issue later led to several official inquiries.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 298

name: Knesset establishes Holocaust remembrance on 27 Nisan
note: Israel's parliament designated 27 Nisan for national remembrance of the Holocaust and its Jewish victims.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 298

name: Soviet authorities execute Jewish Yiddish cultural figures
note: A major Soviet execution of Jewish intellectuals and Yiddish writers as part of Stalinist repression of Jewish culture.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 298

name: West Germany agrees to reparations for Nazi persecution and Jewish property losses
note: West Germany reached reparations arrangements with Israel and Jewish claims representatives; Nachum Goldmann played a major negotiating role.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 298

name: Israel begins receiving West German reparations payments
note: Israel ultimately received about $845 million over fourteen years under the reparations agreement.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 298

name: Chazon Ish dies in Bnei Brak
note: R. Avraham Yeshaya Karelitz, the Chazon Ish, died after becoming one of the most influential halachic authorities in Israel.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 298

name: R. Isser Zalman Meltzer dies in Jerusalem
note: The rosh yeshiva and author of Even HaEzel died three weeks after the Chazon Ish.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 298

name: Cross-border fedayeen attacks contribute to rising Israeli casualties
note: Approximately 1,300 Jews killed since 1949 by Arab infiltrators and cross-border attacks, many originating from Egyptian-controlled areas.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 298

name: Egypt nationalizes the Suez Canal and blocks Israeli shipping routes
note: President Gamal Abdel Nasser nationalized the Suez Canal amid a broader regional confrontation and restrictions affecting Israeli shipping.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 298

name: Israel invades Sinai in the Suez Crisis
note: Israeli forces entered Sinai and rapidly defeated Egyptian forces during the Suez Crisis.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 298

name: Israeli forces withdraw from Sinai under international pressure
note: Following pressure principally from the United States and Soviet Union, Israel withdrew and UN forces were deployed as a buffer.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 298

name: Codex records 171 Israeli soldiers killed in the Sinai campaign
note: 171 Israeli military deaths during the 1956 campaign.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 298

name: Hungarian Jewish refugees flee after the failed uprising
note: Many Hungarian Jews left the country during and after the Soviet suppression of the Hungarian Revolution.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 298

name: Who Is a Jew registration controversy erupts in Israel
note: A government proposal to register as Jewish people who self-identified as Jews without halachically accepted certification triggered a major religious and political controversy.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 298

name: New Jerusalem water reservoir improves city supply
note: A new reservoir was opened to strengthen Jerusalem's water supply after the severe shortages experienced during the 1948 siege.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 299

name: Jewish population of Israel reaches about 1.8 million
note: Approximately 1.8 million Jews living in Israel, an increase of more than one million in eleven years.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 299

name: First volume of Igrot Moshe is published
note: R. Moshe Feinstein published the first volume of Igrot Moshe, one of the most influential modern collections of halachic responsa.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 299

name: Gershon Jacobson questions Nikita Khrushchev about Soviet treatment of Jews
note: An impromptu interview in which journalist Gershon Jacobson challenged Khrushchev on Soviet restrictions and Jewish emigration.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 299

name: Agadir earthquake kills hundreds of Moroccan Jews
note: Agadir earthquake kills hundreds of Moroccan Jews.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 299

name: Mass migration empties most of Morocco's Jewish community
note: By this period more than half of Morocco's roughly 250,000 Jews had settled in Israel, and within a few years most remaining Jews left, many for France.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 299

name: Most Algerian Jews leave for France, with a smaller migration to Israel
note: Of roughly 130,000 Algerian Jews, about 7,700 settled in Israel and most of the remainder migrated to France.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 299

name: Israeli agents capture Adolf Eichmann in Argentina
note: Israeli security agents captured Nazi deportation organizer Adolf Eichmann in Argentina and brought him to Israel for trial.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 299

name: Yuri Gagarin becomes the first human in space
note: The Soviet cosmonaut became the first person to travel into outer space.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 299

name: Adolf Eichmann is tried in Jerusalem
note: Eichmann's televised trial heard extensive survivor testimony and brought renewed international attention to the Holocaust.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 299

name: Adolf Eichmann is executed after conviction in Israel
note: After conviction for crimes against the Jewish people, crimes against humanity and war crimes, Eichmann was executed.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 299

name: R. Aharon Kotler dies
note: R. Aharon Kotler, a major Torah leader in the United States and Israel, died on 2 Kislev.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 299

name: Palestine Liberation Organization is established
note: Arab governments and Palestinian representatives created the Palestine Liberation Organization as a political and military framework for Palestinian nationalism.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 299

name: Fatah emerges as an independent Palestinian armed movement
note: Fatah developing separately from the newly established PLO as a more militant armed organization.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 299

name: Martin Buber dies
note: The philosopher Martin Buber, influential in presenting Hasidic thought and stories to modern Western Jewish audiences, died.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 299

name: Egypt removes the UN Emergency Force from Sinai and masses troops
note: In the May 1967 crisis Egypt demanded withdrawal of UNEF and deployed large forces in Sinai, sharply escalating regional tensions.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 299

name: Egypt closes the Straits of Tiran to Israeli shipping
note: Egypt closed the Straits of Tiran to Israeli shipping, a central step in the crisis preceding the Six-Day War.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 299

name: Israel launches preemptive air strikes and the Six-Day War begins
note: Israel attacked Egyptian airfields and then fought Egypt, Jordan and Syria in a six-day war that transformed the territorial and political map of the region.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 300

name: Israel captures East Jerusalem and the Old City
note: Israeli forces took East Jerusalem and the Old City from Jordanian forces during the Six-Day War.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 300

name: Jews regain access to the Western Wall
note: For the first time since 1948, Jews could freely visit the Western Wall after Israeli forces captured the Old City.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 300

name: Israel occupies the West Bank, Gaza, Sinai and Golan Heights
note: By the end of the Six-Day War Israel controlled the West Bank, East Jerusalem, Gaza Strip, Sinai Peninsula and Golan Heights.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 300

name: Codex records 777 Israeli soldiers killed in the Six-Day War
note: 777 Israeli military deaths in the war.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 300

name: Diaspora Jews mobilize volunteers and support for Israel during the Six-Day War
note: A major wave of worldwide Jewish fundraising, volunteering and travel to Israel during the crisis and war.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 300

name: Post-1967 baal teshuva movement expands
note: The emotional and religious impact of the Six-Day War is associated with a long-term increase in Jewish return to religious observance, especially among younger Jews.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 300

name: Adin Steinsaltz publishes first volume of his accessible Talmud edition
note: R. Adin Steinsaltz began publishing a modern annotated edition of the Talmud designed to broaden accessibility.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 300

name: Responsa Project begins computerization of rabbinic literature
note: A project began entering responsa and other rabbinic texts into computers for rapid full-text retrieval, an important milestone in digital Jewish scholarship.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 300

name: Apollo 8 astronauts read Genesis from lunar orbit
note: During a broadcast from lunar orbit, Apollo 8 astronauts read the opening verses of Genesis.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 300

name: Nine Jews are publicly executed in Damascus
note: Nine Jews executed publicly in Damascus.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 300

name: R. Aryeh Levin dies in Jerusalem
note: R. Aryeh Levin, widely known for visiting prisoners, the sick and the poor, died.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 300

name: War of Attrition intensifies along the Suez Canal
note: Egypt began sustained artillery and military operations across the Suez Canal against Israeli positions.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 300

name: Jewish population of Israel reaches about 2.4 million
note: Roughly 2.4 million Jews living in Israel.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 300

name: Libya confiscates Jewish property
note: The Libyan government ordered confiscation of Jewish property.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 300

name: PLO-linked groups make international aircraft hijacking a major tactic
note: Palestinian armed organizations used hijackings and hostage-taking as a prominent form of international terrorism.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 300

name: About one thousand Soviet Jews are permitted to emigrate
note: About 1,000 Jews being permitted to leave the Soviet Union in 1970.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 301

name: Soviet authorities arrest Jews commemorating Babyn Yar
note: Ten Jews were arrested while commemorating the massacre at Babyn Yar, part of continuing Soviet restrictions on Jewish public activity.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 301

name: Soviet Jewish emigration rises to about fourteen thousand five hundred
note: 14,500 Jews permitted to leave the Soviet Union in 1971, part of the growing refusenik and emigration movement.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 301

name: Egypt and Syria attack Israel on Yom Kippur
note: Egyptian and Syrian forces launched a coordinated surprise attack on Israeli positions in Sinai and the Golan Heights.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 301

name: Israeli counteroffensive crosses the Suez Canal
note: After severe early setbacks, Israeli forces counterattacked and crossed to the west bank of the Suez Canal.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 301

name: UN-backed ceasefire ends major fighting in the Yom Kippur War
note: International diplomacy produced a ceasefire after roughly three weeks of fighting.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 301

name: Codex records 2,522 Israeli soldiers killed in the Yom Kippur War
note: 2,522 Israeli military deaths.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 301

name: Arab oil embargo follows the Yom Kippur War
note: Arab oil-producing states used oil exports as political leverage against countries seen as supporting Israel.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 301

name: Gush Emunim begins settlement activism in territories captured in 1967
note: Religious-nationalist activists associated with Gush Emunim established a settlement initiative in territory captured from Syria and advocated Jewish settlement throughout areas captured in 1967.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 301

name: About one hundred thousand Soviet Jews have immigrated to Israel since 1967
note: Roughly 100,000 Soviet Jews arriving in Israel during the post-1967 emigration wave.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 301

name: Major Torah centers are rebuilt in Israel and the United States
note: The rapid post-Holocaust rebuilding of yeshivot and Torah institutions in Israel and especially the New York area.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 301

name: Air France Flight 139 is hijacked and Jewish and Israeli passengers are held at Entebbe
note: Hijackers diverted an Air France flight to Uganda and separated many Israeli and Jewish passengers from others, holding them as hostages.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 301

name: Israeli forces rescue hostages at Entebbe
note: Israeli commandos flew thousands of kilometers to Entebbe, rescued most of the remaining hostages and returned them to Israel; operation commander Yonatan Netanyahu was killed.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 301

name: Beis Yisroel of Ger dies
note: R. Yisrael Alter, the Beis Yisroel of Ger, died and was succeeded by his brother R. Simcha Bunim Alter, the Lev Simcha.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 301

name: Lev Simcha becomes Gerer Rebbe
note: R. Simcha Bunim Alter succeeded his brother as Gerer Rebbe.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 301

name: Egyptian President Anwar Sadat visits Jerusalem
note: Sadat made a historic visit to Jerusalem, opening a new phase of direct Egyptian-Israeli diplomacy.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 301

name: Egypt and Israel sign a peace treaty
note: President Anwar Sadat and Prime Minister Menachem Begin signed the Egypt-Israel peace treaty, witnessed by U.S. President Jimmy Carter.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 301

name: Israel agrees to withdraw forces and settlements from Sinai under the peace treaty
note: The treaty provided for phased Israeli withdrawal from Sinai and normalization of relations with Egypt.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 301

name: Menachem Begin visits Cairo after the peace agreement
note: The Israeli prime minister visited Cairo as Egyptian-Israeli relations moved toward normalization.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 301

name: Satmar Rebbe R. Yoel Teitelbaum dies
note: R. Yoel Teitelbaum, a leading anti-Zionist Hasidic figure, died and was succeeded by his nephew R. Moshe Teitelbaum.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 301

name: R. Joseph Breuer dies in New York
note: R. Joseph Breuer, leader of the Washington Heights Orthodox community preserving Frankfurt communal traditions, died at age 98.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 302

name: R. Shimon Schwab succeeds R. Joseph Breuer
note: R. Shimon Schwab became the principal rabbinic successor in the German Orthodox kehilla.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 302

name: Palestinian gunmen kill Jewish students in Hebron
note: Seven Jewish students were killed and sixteen wounded in an attack in Hebron.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 302

name: Israeli authorities deport the Arab mayor of Hebron for incitement
note: Israeli authorities deport the Arab mayor of Hebron for incitement.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 302

name: Soviet Jewish emigration rises sharply in the late 1970s
note: 17,000 Jews leaving in 1977, 29,000 in 1978 and 51,500 in 1979, with fewer than half settling in Israel.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 302

name: Large Israeli emigrant community develops in the United States
note: Large Israeli emigrant community develops in the United States.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 302

name: Israel destroys Iraq's Osirak nuclear reactor
note: Israeli aircraft bombed and destroyed the Iraqi nuclear reactor at Osirak, arguing that it posed a future security threat.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 302

name: Artillery shelling of northern Israel kills three Jews
note: Three Jews killed and seventeen wounded by heavy shelling of the Galilee.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 302

name: Israel dismantles Jewish settlements in northern Sinai
note: As the Egypt-Israel peace treaty was implemented, Israeli settlements in Sinai were evacuated and dismantled, sometimes against resistance by settlers.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 302

name: Israeli diplomat is assassinated in Paris
note: An Israeli diplomat killed by terrorists in Paris.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 302

name: Israel invades Lebanon in Operation Peace for Galilee
note: Israeli forces entered Lebanon after prolonged cross-border violence and attacks involving PLO forces based there.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 302

name: PLO forces evacuate Beirut
note: After Israeli forces reached and besieged Beirut, PLO fighters withdrew under an internationally mediated arrangement.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 302

name: Israeli forces begin a prolonged partial occupation of southern Lebanon
note: Israel later withdrew from much of Lebanon but maintained a southern security zone for years.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 302

name: Skulener Rebbe R. Eliezer Zusia Portugal dies
note: The Skulener Rebbe, known for religious and welfare institutions in Romania, Israel and the United States, died.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 302

name: Reform rabbis adopt patrilineal descent policy under specified conditions
note: The Reform movement's rabbinic body accepted children of one Jewish parent as Jewish when raised with affirmative acts of Jewish identification.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 302

name: Jewish Theological Seminary votes to ordain women as rabbis
note: The Conservative movement's seminary approved training and ordination of women, prompting some senior traditionalist scholars to leave.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 302

name: Israel exchanges thousands of prisoners for six soldiers
note: 4,600 prisoners exchanged for six Israeli soldiers.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 302

name: Baba Sali dies in Israel
note: R. Yisrael Abuhatzeira, the Baba Sali, died on 4 Shevat.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 302

name: Jerusalem's Jewish population reaches about 320,000
note: Roughly 320,000 Jewish residents in Jerusalem and about 445,000 residents overall.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 302

name: Tel Aviv metropolitan population reaches about 800,000
note: Roughly 800,000 residents for the Tel Aviv metropolitan area.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 303

name: Operation Moses brings thousands of Ethiopian Jews toward Israel
note: Operation Moses brings thousands of Ethiopian Jews toward Israel.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 304

name: Israel withdraws most forces from Lebanon
note: The completion of the main withdrawal from Lebanon three years after the 1982 invasion.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 303

name: Codex records 654 Israeli soldiers killed during the Lebanon campaign
note: 654 Israeli military deaths, noting that many were killed in attacks rather than conventional battles.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 303

name: Israel exchanges 1,150 prisoners for three soldiers
note: A major prisoner exchange.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 303

name: Egyptian soldier kills seven Israeli tourists in Sinai
note: An Egyptian soldier opened fire on Israeli tourists in Sinai, killing seven.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 303

name: Achille Lauro hijackers murder Leon Klinghoffer
note: Palestinian hijackers seized the Italian cruise ship Achille Lauro and murdered Jewish American passenger Leon Klinghoffer.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 303

name: Anatoly Sharansky is released from Soviet prison and immigrates to Israel
note: Prominent Soviet Jewish refusenik Anatoly Sharansky was released and allowed to emigrate to Israel.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 303

name: Elie Wiesel receives the Nobel Peace Prize
note: Holocaust survivor and writer Elie Wiesel received the Nobel Peace Prize for his work on memory, human rights and moral responsibility.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 303

name: Pope John Paul II visits Rome's Great Synagogue
note: John Paul II became the first pope in modern times to make an official visit to a synagogue in Rome.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 303

name: Neve Shalom Synagogue attack kills worshippers in Istanbul
note: Attackers killed 22 worshippers at Istanbul's Neve Shalom Synagogue.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 303

name: Gorbachev announces liberalization of Soviet political controls
note: Soviet reforms loosened decades of restrictions and opened greater space for Jewish religious, cultural and emigration activity.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 303

name: Jewish religious education expands openly in the late Soviet Union
note: Visitors and local activists established classes, schools and yeshiva activity as state controls weakened.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 303

name: Rising nationalism and economic insecurity accelerate Jewish emigration from the USSR
note: Rising nationalism and economic insecurity accelerate Jewish emigration from the USSR.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 303

name: United States bars Austrian President Kurt Waldheim
note: The United States placed Kurt Waldheim on a watch list after evidence concerning his wartime service and knowledge of Nazi atrocities became public.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 303

name: Night of the Gliders attack kills six Israeli soldiers
note: An armed infiltrator crossed from Lebanon by hang glider and attacked an Israeli military camp, killing six soldiers.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 303

name: First Intifada begins
note: A Palestinian uprising against Israeli rule began in the West Bank and Gaza and continued for several years.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 303

name: Nitei Gavriel begins publication
note: R. Gavriel Zinner began publishing Nitei Gavriel, a large contemporary collection of halachic laws and customs.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 303

name: Tel Aviv–Jerusalem bus attack sends bus into a ravine
note: A Palestinian attacker seized control of a bus on the Jerusalem–Tel Aviv route and forced it into a ravine.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 303

name: Iraq invades Kuwait and threatens attacks on Israel
note: Iraq occupied Kuwait and threatened Israel if an international coalition attacked Iraqi forces.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 303

name: Meir Kahane is assassinated in New York
note: Rabbi and political activist Meir Kahane was assassinated after a speech in New York.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 304

name: Iraq fires Scud missiles at Israel during the Gulf War
note: Iraq launched 39 conventional-warhead missiles at Israel during the U.S.-led campaign to expel Iraqi forces from Kuwait.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 304

name: Lubavitcher Rebbe intensifies public emphasis on imminent redemption
note: A marked increase in R. Menachem Mendel Schneerson's public statements about the imminence of Mashiach and growing messianic identification among some followers.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 304

name: Operation Solomon airlifts about fifteen thousand Ethiopian Jews to Israel
note: A rapid airlift brought roughly 14,000–15,000 Ethiopian Jews to Israel in little more than a day.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 304

name: Crown Heights riot kills Yankel Rosenbaum
note: Days of racial and communal violence followed a fatal traffic accident in Crown Heights; Jewish student Yankel Rosenbaum was stabbed and died.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 304

name: Communist Party monopoly collapses in the Soviet Union
note: The failed August coup and the collapse of Communist Party rule accelerated the dissolution of the Soviet political system.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 304

name: Germany offers settlement to Jews leaving the former Soviet Union
note: A German policy allowing Jews from the former Soviet Union to settle as part of rebuilding Jewish communities destroyed in the Holocaust.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 304

name: Madrid Peace Conference opens direct Arab-Israeli negotiations
note: Israel, Arab states and a joint Jordanian-Palestinian delegation met under U.S. and Soviet sponsorship to launch bilateral and multilateral peace talks.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 304

name: Israeli Embassy in Buenos Aires is bombed
note: A car bomb destroyed the Israeli embassy, killing 29 people and injuring hundreds.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 304

name: Soviet Union's dissolution reshapes Jewish life and migration
note: The USSR was replaced by independent successor states, accelerating political change and large-scale Jewish emigration.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 304

name: Lev Simcha of Ger dies
note: R. Simcha Bunim Alter, the Lev Simcha, died and was succeeded by his half-brother R. Pinchas Menachem Alter.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 304

name: Pnei Menachem becomes Gerer Rebbe
note: R. Pinchas Menachem Alter succeeded as Gerer Rebbe.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 304

name: About 350,000 Jews from the former Soviet Union settle in Israel over three years
note: Roughly 350,000 immigrants from the former Soviet Union arriving in Israel during the preceding three years.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 304

name: Jewish population of Israel reaches about 4.25 million
note: Approximately 4.25 million Jewish residents in Israel.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 304

name: Secret Oslo negotiations produce a Declaration of Principles
note: Israeli and PLO representatives negotiated secretly in Norway and initialed a framework for Palestinian interim self-government.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 304

name: Israel and PLO publicly sign the Oslo Declaration of Principles
note: The agreement was formally signed in Washington on 13 September 1993 after mutual recognition between Israel and the PLO.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 304

name: Chief Rabbi Yisrael Meir Lau meets Pope John Paul II in Rome
note: Israel's Ashkenazi Chief Rabbi met Pope John Paul II.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 305

name: Baruch Goldstein kills twenty-nine Muslim worshippers in Hebron
note: Israeli Jewish physician Baruch Goldstein opened fire on Muslim worshippers at the Cave of the Patriarchs/Ibrahimi Mosque, killing 29 before he was killed.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 305

name: Brooklyn Bridge shooting kills Ari Halberstam
note: A gunman fired on a van carrying Jewish students near the Brooklyn Bridge, killing 16-year-old Ari Halberstam and wounding others.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 305

name: Lubavitcher Rebbe R. Menachem Mendel Schneerson dies
note: The seventh Lubavitcher Rebbe died after decades of global institutional expansion through Chabad emissaries.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 305

name: AMIA Jewish community center bombing kills eighty-five people
note: A bombing destroyed the AMIA Jewish community center in Buenos Aires, killing 85 people and wounding hundreds.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 305

name: Israel and Jordan sign the Washington Declaration ending the state of belligerency
note: Israel and Jordan formally declared an end to the state of belligerency, paving the way for the full peace treaty signed later that year.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 305

name: Tel Aviv bus suicide bombing kills twenty-two people
note: A Hamas suicide bomber attacked a crowded bus in Tel Aviv, killing 22 people.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 305

name: R. Shlomo Carlebach dies
note: Singer, composer and rabbi Shlomo Carlebach died, leaving a major influence on modern Jewish liturgical and communal music.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 305

name: Israel establishes a state commission on the Yemenite children affair
note: A state commission of inquiry was established to investigate longstanding allegations concerning the disappearance of children, especially from Yemenite immigrant families, during the early years of the state.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 306

name: R. Shlomo Zalman Auerbach dies in Jerusalem
note: R. Shlomo Zalman Auerbach, one of the leading halachic decisors and roshei yeshiva of the postwar period, died in Jerusalem.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 306

name: Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin is assassinated in Tel Aviv
note: Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin was shot and killed by Yigal Amir after a peace rally in Tel Aviv, a political assassination that deeply affected Israeli society.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 306

name: Jerusalem bus 18 suicide bombing kills twenty-six people
note: A suicide bomber attacked bus number 18 near Jerusalem's central bus station; 24 people died at the scene and two more later died from their wounds.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 306

name: Second Jerusalem bus 18 suicide bombing kills nineteen people
note: One week later another suicide bomber attacked bus number 18 in central Jerusalem, killing nineteen people.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 306

name: Dizengoff Center suicide bombing kills thirteen people
note: A suicide bombing outside Dizengoff Center during the Purim period killed thirteen people and wounded many others.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 306

name: Pnei Menachem of Ger dies
note: R. Pinchas Menachem Alter, the Pnei Menachem and Gerer Rebbe, died.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 306

name: R. Yisrael Aryeh Alter succeeds as Gerer Rebbe
note: R. Yisrael Aryeh Alter succeeded his uncle R. Pinchas Menachem Alter as Gerer Rebbe.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 306

name: Christoph Meili preserves Holocaust-era Swiss bank records from destruction
note: Swiss security guard Christoph Meili removed and preserved documents he believed related to wartime or dormant-account records after finding them marked for destruction, helping intensify public scrutiny of Holocaust-era Swiss financial assets.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 306

name: Jordanian soldier kills seven Israeli schoolgirls at Naharayim
note: A Jordanian soldier opened fire on an Israeli school group at the Island of Peace/Naharayim, killing seven girls and wounding others.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 306

name: Café Apropo suicide bombing kills three women in Tel Aviv
note: A suicide bomber attacked Café Apropo in Tel Aviv, killing three women and wounding dozens.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 306

name: Mahane Yehuda double suicide bombing kills sixteen people
note: Two suicide bombers attacked Jerusalem's Mahane Yehuda market, killing sixteen people and wounding many others.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 306

name: Ben Yehuda pedestrian-mall suicide bombings kill five people
note: Three suicide bombers attacked the Ben Yehuda pedestrian mall in Jerusalem, killing five people and wounding many others.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 306

name: Swiss banks agree to a $1.25 billion Holocaust-era settlement
note: Swiss banks and class-action plaintiffs reached a $1.25 billion settlement covering Holocaust-related claims, including dormant deposits and other categories of victims and claimants.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 306

name: Reform rabbis adopt a new Statement of Principles in Pittsburgh
note: The Central Conference of American Rabbis adopted a Statement of Principles for Reform Judaism that placed renewed emphasis on Torah study, mitzvot and Jewish religious practice while retaining Reform commitments to autonomy and pluralism.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 306

name: Pope John Paul II makes a Jubilee pilgrimage to the Holy Land
note: Pope John Paul II visited Jordan, Israel and the Palestinian territories, including Yad Vashem, Jerusalem's chief rabbis and the Western Wall.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 307

name: British High Court rejects David Irving's libel claim against Deborah Lipstadt and Penguin
note: The High Court rejected Holocaust denier David Irving's libel suit and upheld the defendants' core criticisms of his historical methods and Holocaust denial.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 307

name: Israel withdraws its forces from southern Lebanon
note: Israel completed a unilateral military withdrawal from southern Lebanon to the international border after years of occupation and security-zone warfare.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 307

name: Bobover Rebbe R. Shlomo Halberstam dies
note: R. Shlomo Halberstam, who rebuilt the Bobov Hasidic dynasty in the United States after surviving the Holocaust, died.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 307

name: R. Naftali Tzvi Halberstam succeeds in Bobov
note: R. Naftali Tzvi Halberstam succeeded his father as a principal Bobover Rebbe.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 307

name: Camp David summit ends without an Israeli-Palestinian final-status agreement
note: President Bill Clinton, Prime Minister Ehud Barak and Palestinian Authority Chairman Yasser Arafat held intensive final-status negotiations at Camp David but did not bridge differences over borders, Jerusalem, refugees and other core issues.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 307

name: Joseph Lieberman is selected as the Democratic vice-presidential nominee
note: U.S. Senator Joseph Lieberman became the first openly observant Orthodox Jew nominated for vice president by a major American political party.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 307

name: Ariel Sharon visits the Temple Mount / Haram al-Sharif
note: Likud opposition leader Ariel Sharon visited the Temple Mount/Haram al-Sharif under heavy police protection amid intense Israeli-Palestinian tensions.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 307

name: Second Intifada begins
note: Large-scale Israeli-Palestinian protests, clashes and violence erupted at the end of September 2000 and developed into the Second, or al-Aqsa, Intifada.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 307

name: Israeli forces withdraw from Joseph's Tomb in Nablus during early Intifada fighting
note: Israeli forces withdrew from Joseph's Tomb after sustained clashes and an agreement concerning security at the site.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 307

name: Joseph's Tomb is vandalized after the Israeli withdrawal
note: The religious site was damaged and vandalized after Israeli forces withdrew.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 307

name: Codex records a worldwide surge in attacks on Jewish targets
note: More than 200 attacks on Jewish targets worldwide during Tishrei 5761, including more than 60 attacks on synagogues.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 307

name: Binyamin and Talia Kahane are killed in a shooting attack
note: Binyamin Zeev Kahane and his wife Talia were killed when gunmen fired on their vehicle on a West Bank road; several of their children were injured.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 307

name: More than 230,000 Jews from the former Soviet Union immigrate to the United States during the 1990s
note: 231,680 Jewish immigrants from the former Soviet Union to the United States between 1991 and 2000, including 105,598 settling in the New York area.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 307

name: R. Mordechai Gifter dies
note: R. Mordechai Gifter, a leading rosh yeshiva associated with Telz in Cleveland, died.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 308

name: R. Avigdor Miller dies in New York
note: R. Avigdor Miller, a prolific Orthodox rabbi, lecturer and author, died in New York.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 308

name: Sbarro restaurant suicide bombing kills fifteen people in Jerusalem
note: A Hamas suicide bomber attacked the crowded Sbarro restaurant in central Jerusalem, killing fifteen people and wounding more than one hundred.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 308

name: R. Avraham Yaakov Pam dies
note: R. Avraham Yaakov Pam, rosh yeshiva of Torah Vodaath and an influential Orthodox communal leader, died.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 308

name: September 11 attacks destroy the World Trade Center and strike the Pentagon
note: Al-Qaeda hijackers attacked the World Trade Center and Pentagon; a fourth hijacked aircraft crashed in Pennsylvania after passengers resisted. The attacks killed 2,977 victims.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 308

name: Israeli minister Rehavam Ze'evi is assassinated in Jerusalem
note: Tourism Minister Rehavam Ze'evi was assassinated by members of the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 307

name: R. Elazar Menachem Man Shach dies in Bnei Brak
note: R. Elazar Menachem Man Shach, one of the leading Lithuanian-haredi roshei yeshiva and public leaders of the late twentieth century, died.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 308

name: Massive funeral is held for R. Shach
note: A very large crowd attended R. Shach's funeral in Bnei Brak.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 308

name: United States begins military operations in Afghanistan after the September 11 attacks
note: The U.S.-led intervention in Afghanistan began after the September 11 attacks and the Taliban government's refusal to surrender al-Qaeda leaders.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 308

name: Israeli navy intercepts the Karine A weapons ship
note: Israeli naval forces intercepted the Karine A, which was carrying a large shipment of weapons that Israel said was intended for Palestinian forces.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 308

name: Wafa Idris carries out a suicide bombing in Jerusalem
note: A female suicide bomber detonated an explosive device on Jaffa Road, killing one person and wounding dozens.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 308

name: Passover Seder massacre at Netanya's Park Hotel kills thirty people
note: A Hamas suicide bomber attacked a Passover Seder at the Park Hotel in Netanya, killing thirty people and injuring about 160.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 309

name: Jewish population of Israel reaches about 5.3 million
note: Approximately 5.3 million Jews living in Israel in Iyar 5762.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 309

name: Large group of North American immigrants arrives in Israel together
note: A then-record group of about 400 North American immigrants arriving together to settle in Israel.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 309

name: Codex records a Second Intifada casualty and attack snapshot
note: 13,421 attacks from the beginning of the Second Intifada through 14 Tammuz 5762, with 561 killed and 4,208 injured.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 309

name: Ilan Ramon flies as Israel's first astronaut and carries Jewish artifacts into space
note: Israeli Air Force colonel Ilan Ramon flew aboard Space Shuttle Columbia as Israel's first astronaut. He carried Jewish and Holocaust-related objects, including a miniature Torah scroll associated with a Bergen-Belsen survivor.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 309

name: Space Shuttle Columbia disintegrates during re-entry, killing Ilan Ramon and the crew
note: Columbia was lost during re-entry over the southern United States, killing all seven crew members, including Ilan Ramon.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 309

name: United States and coalition invade Iraq
note: A U.S.-led coalition invaded Iraq and overthrew Saddam Hussein's government.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 308

name: Truck bombs attack Neve Shalom and Beth Israel synagogues in Istanbul
note: Two suicide truck bombs exploded outside the Neve Shalom and Beth Israel synagogues during Shabbat, killing worshippers, passersby and the attackers and wounding hundreds.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 309

name: Codex compares Israeli road deaths with war and security deaths since 1948
note: A cumulative comparison of 22,700 deaths in road accidents and 21,600 deaths in wars and security-related incidents since Israel's establishment.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 309

name: Construction of the West Bank barrier expands during the Second Intifada
note: Israel continued building a barrier of fences and walls along and within the West Bank, arguing that it was intended to reduce attacks; the route and humanitarian effects were highly controversial.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 309

name: Codex records a 44 percent fall in Israeli terrorism casualties during 2004
note: Casualties from terrorism fell by 44% compared with the previous year while construction of the barrier was still incomplete.
source: Chronological Index of Jewish History, p. 309
